Name: CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0
Description: The CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark provides prescriptive guidance for establishing a secure baseline configuration for Microsoft Azure. This Benchmark is scoped to establish foundational security for tenancy in the Microsoft Azure cloud services platform.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'security defaults' is Enabled in Microsoft Entra ID

Attributes.Description: [**IMPORTANT - Please read the section overview:** If your organization pays for Microsoft Entra ID licensing (included in Microsoft 365 E3, E5, F5, or Business Premium, and EM&S E3 or E5 licenses) and can use Conditional Access, ignore the recommendations in this section and proceed to the Conditional Access section.]  Security defaults in Microsoft Entra ID make it easier to be secure and help protect your organization. Security defaults contain preconfigured security settings for common attacks.  Security defaults is available to everyone. The goal is to ensure that all organizations have a basic level of security enabled at no extra cost. You may turn on security defaults in the Azure portal.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Security defaults provide secure default settings that we manage on behalf of organizations to keep customers safe until they are ready to manage their own identity security settings.  For example, doing the following:  - Requiring all users and admins to register for MFA. - Challenging users with MFA - when necessary, based on factors such as location, device, role, and task. - Disabling authentication from legacy authentication clients, which can’t do MFA.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: This recommendation should be implemented initially and then may be overridden by other service/product specific CIS Benchmarks. Administrators should also be aware that certain configurations in Microsoft Entra ID may impact other Microsoft services such as Microsoft 365.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Note:** These steps require at least the Conditional Access Administrator role.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  To enable security defaults in your directory:  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Browse to `Microsoft Entra ID` > `Properties`. 3. Select `Manage security defaults`. 4. Under `Security defaults`, select `Enabled`. 5. Select `Save`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  ``` az rest --method patch --url 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy' --body '{"isEnabled":true}' az rest --method get --url 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy' --query "isEnabled" ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  ``` Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Policy.Read.All", "Policy.ReadWrite.SecurityDefaults" Update-MgPolicyIdentitySecurityDefaultEnforcementPolicy -IsEnabled:$true (Get-MgPolicyIdentitySecurityDefaultEnforcementPolicy).IsEnabled ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  To ensure security defaults is enabled in your directory:  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Browse to `Microsoft Entra ID` > `Properties`. 3. Select `Manage security defaults`. 4. Under `Security defaults`, verify that `Enabled` is selected.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  ``` az rest --method get --url 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy' --query "isEnabled" ```  Ensure the returned value is `true`.  **Audit from PowerShell**  ``` Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Policy.Read.All" (Get-MgPolicyIdentitySecurityDefaultEnforcementPolicy).IsEnabled ```  Ensure the returned value is `True`.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: This recommendation differs from the [Microsoft 365 Benchmark](https://workbench.cisecurity.org/benchmarks/5741). This is because the potential impact associated with disabling Security Defaults is dependent upon the security settings implemented in the environment. It is recommended that organizations disabling Security Defaults implement appropriate security settings to replace the settings configured by Security Defaults.
Attributes.DefaultValue: If your tenant was created on or after October 22, 2019, security defaults may already be enabled in your tenant.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Require Multifactor Authentication to register or join devices with Microsoft Entra' is set to 'Yes'

Attributes.Description: **Note:** This recommendation is only relevant if your subscription is using Per-User MFA. If your organization is licensed to use Conditional Access, the preferred method of requiring MFA to join devices to Entra ID is to use a Conditional Access policy (see additional information below for link).  Joining or registering devices to Microsoft Entra ID should require multi-factor authentication.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Multi-factor authentication is recommended when adding devices to Microsoft Entra ID. When set to `Yes`, users who are adding devices from the internet must first use the second method of authentication before their device is successfully added to the directory. This ensures that rogue devices are not added to the domain using a compromised user account.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: A slight impact of additional overhead, as Administrators will now have to approve every access to the domain.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu 2. Select `Microsoft Entra ID` 3. Under `Manage`, select `Devices` 4. Under `Manage`, select `Device settings` 5. Under `Microsoft Entra join and registration settings`, set `Require Multifactor Authentication to register or join devices with Microsoft Entra` to `Yes` 6. Click `Save`
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu 2. Select `Microsoft Entra ID` 3. Under `Manage`, select `Devices` 4. Under `Manage`, select `Device settings` 5. Under `Microsoft Entra join and registration settings`, ensure that `Require Multifactor Authentication to register or join devices with Microsoft Entra` is set to `Yes`
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: If Conditional Access is available, this recommendation should be bypassed in favor of the Conditional Access implementation of requiring Multifactor Authentication to register or join devices with Microsoft Entra.  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-registration
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, `Require Multifactor Authentication to register or join devices with Microsoft Entra` is set to `No`.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Per-user MFA' Status is 'Enabled' or 'Enforced' for All Users

Attributes.Description: [**IMPORTANT - Please read the section overview:** If your organization pays for Microsoft Entra ID licensing (included in Microsoft 365 E3, E5, F5, or Business Premium, and EM&S E3 or E5 licenses) and can use Conditional Access, ignore the recommendations in this section and proceed to the Conditional Access section.]  Enable multifactor authentication for all users.  **Note:** Since 2024, Azure has been rolling out mandatory multifactor authentication. For more information:  - https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/announcing-mandatory-multi-factor-authentication-for-azure-sign-in - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Multifactor authentication requires an individual to present a minimum of two separate forms of authentication before access is granted. Multifactor authentication provides additional assurance that the individual attempting to gain access is who they claim to be. With multifactor authentication, an attacker would need to compromise at least two different authentication mechanisms, increasing the difficulty of compromise and thus reducing the risk.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Users would require two forms of authentication before any access is granted. Additional administrative time will be required for managing dual forms of authentication when enabling multifactor authentication.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Note:** These steps require at least the Authentication Policy Administrator role.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Entra ID`. 2. Under `Manage`, click `Users`. 3. Click `Per-user MFA` from the top menu. 4. Click the box next to a user with `Status` `Disabled`. 5. Click `Enable MFA`. 6. Click `Enable`. 7. Repeat steps 4-6 for each user requiring remediation.  **Other options within Azure Portal**  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/tutorial-enable-azure-mfa - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-mfasettings - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-old-require-mfa-admin - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-getstarted#enable-multi-factor-authentication-with-conditional-access  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Run the following commands, repeating the second command for each user whose status is `disabled`:  ``` Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod" Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method PATCH -Uri "/beta/users/<user-principal-name>/authentication/requirements" -Body '{"perUserMfaState":"enabled"}' -ContentType "application/json" ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Note:** Reading another user's per-user MFA status requires at least the Global Reader or Authentication Policy Administrator role.  **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Entra ID`. 2. Under `Manage`, click `Users`. 3. Click `Per-user MFA` from the top menu. 4. Ensure that `Status` is `Enabled` or `Enforced` for all users.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Per-user MFA status is available only from the Microsoft Graph beta API. Run the following commands to list each user whose status is neither `enabled` nor `enforced`:  ``` Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "User.ReadBasic.All", "Policy.Read.All" Get-MgUser -All -Property Id, UserPrincipalName | ForEach-Object { $state = (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri "/beta/users/$($_.Id)/authentication/requirements").perUserMfaState if ($state -notin 'enabled', 'enforced') { [pscustomobject]@{ UserPrincipalName = $_.UserPrincipalName; PerUserMfaState = $state } } } ```  If any user is returned, this recommendation is non-compliant.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: A user whose status is `Enabled` moves to `Enforced` automatically after registering a multifactor authentication method, so both statuses satisfy this recommendation.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, every user's per-user MFA status is `Disabled`.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Allow users to remember multifactor authentication on devices they trust' is Disabled

Attributes.Description: [**IMPORTANT - Please read the section overview:** If your organization pays for Microsoft Entra ID licensing (included in Microsoft 365 E3, E5, F5, or Business Premium, and EM&S E3 or E5 licenses) and can use Conditional Access, ignore the recommendations in this section and proceed to the Conditional Access section.]  Do not allow users to remember multi-factor authentication on devices.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Remembering Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for devices and browsers allows users to have the option to bypass MFA for a set number of days after performing a successful sign-in using MFA. This can enhance usability by minimizing the number of times a user may need to perform two-step verification on the same device. However, if an account or device is compromised, remembering MFA for trusted devices may affect security. Hence, it is recommended that users not be allowed to bypass MFA.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: For every login attempt, the user will be required to perform multi-factor authentication.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu 2. Select `Microsoft Entra ID` 3. Under `Manage`, click `Users` 4. Click the `Per-user MFA` button on the top bar 5. Click on `Service settings` 6. Uncheck the box next to `Allow users to remember multi-factor authentication on devices they trust` 7. Click `Save`
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu 2. Select `Microsoft Entra ID` 3. Under `Manage`, click `Users` 4. Click the `Per-user MFA` button on the top bar 5. Click on `Service settings` 6. Ensure that `Allow users to remember multi-factor authentication on devices they trust` is not enabled
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, `Allow users to remember multi-factor authentication on devices they trust` is disabled.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that Azure Admin Accounts Are Not Used for Daily Operations

Attributes.Description: Microsoft Azure admin accounts should not be used for routine, non-administrative tasks.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Using admin accounts for daily operations increases the risk of accidental misconfigurations and security breaches.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Minor administrative overhead includes managing separate accounts, enforcing stricter access controls, and potential licensing costs for advanced security features.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: If admin accounts are being used for daily operations, consider the following:  - Monitor and alert on unusual activity. - Enforce the principle of least privilege. - Revoke any unnecessary administrative access. - Use Conditional Access to limit access to resources. - Ensure that administrators have separate admin and user accounts. - Use Microsoft Entra ID Protection to detect, investigate, and remediate identity-based risks. - Use Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft Entra ID to limit standing administrator access to privileged roles, discover who has access, and review privileged access.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  Monitor:  1. Go to `Monitor`. 2. Click `Activity log`. 3. Review the activity log and ensure that admin accounts are not being used for daily operations.  Microsoft Entra ID:  1. Go to `Microsoft Entra ID`. 2. Under `Monitoring`, click `Sign-in logs`. 3. Review the sign-in logs and ensure that admin accounts are not being accessed more frequently than necessary.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that Guest Users are Reviewed on a Regular Basis

Attributes.Description: Microsoft Entra ID has native and extended identity functionality allowing you to invite people from outside your organization to be guest users in your cloud account and sign in with their own work, school, or social identities.  While an automated assessment procedure exists for this recommendation, the assessment status remains manual. Evaluating the appropriateness of guest users requires a manual review, as it depends on the specific needs and context of each organization and environment.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Guest users are typically added outside your employee on-boarding/off-boarding process and could potentially be overlooked indefinitely. To prevent this, guest users should be reviewed on a regular basis. During this audit, guest users should also be determined to not have administrative privileges.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Before removing guest users, determine their use and scope. Like removing any user, there may be unforeseen consequences to systems if an account is removed without careful consideration.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu 2. Select `Microsoft Entra ID` 3. Under `Manage`, select `Users` 4. Click on `Add filter` 5. Select `User type` 6. Select `Guest` from the Value dropdown 7. Click `Apply` 8. Check the box next to all `Guest` users that are no longer required or are inactive 9. Click `Delete` 10. Click `OK`  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Before deleting the user, disable it (using the ID from the Audit Procedure) to determine whether any dependent systems rely on it:  ``` az ad user update --id <exampleaccountid@domain.com> --account-enabled false ```  After confirming there are no dependent systems, delete the user:  ``` az ad user delete --id <exampleaccountid@domain.com> ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Before deleting the user, disable it to determine whether any dependent systems rely on it:  ``` Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All' Update-MgUser -UserId <exampleaccountid@domain.com> -AccountEnabled:$false ```  After confirming there are no dependent systems, delete the user:  ``` Remove-MgUser -UserId <exampleaccountid@domain.com> ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu 2. Select `Microsoft Entra ID` 3. Under `Manage`, select `Users` 4. Click on `Add filter` 5. Select `User type` 6. Select `Guest` from the Value dropdown 7. Click `Apply` 8. Audit the listed guest users  **Audit from Azure CLI**  ``` az ad user list --query "[?userType=='Guest']" ```  Ensure all users listed are still required and not inactive.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Connect to Microsoft Graph, then list guest users:  ``` Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.Read.All' Get-MgUser -Filter "userType eq 'Guest'" -All | Select-Object DisplayName, UserPrincipalName, UserType ```  Ensure all guest users listed are still required and not inactive.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [e9ac8f8e-ce22-4355-8f04-99b911d6be52](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2Fe9ac8f8e-ce22-4355-8f04-99b911d6be52) **- Name:** 'Guest accounts with read permissions on Azure resources should be removed' - **Policy ID:** [94e1c2ac-cbbe-4cac-a2b5-389c812dee87](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F94e1c2ac-cbbe-4cac-a2b5-389c812dee87) **- Name:** 'Guest accounts with write permissions on Azure resources should be removed' - **Policy ID:** [339353f6-2387-4a45-abe4-7f529d121046](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F339353f6-2387-4a45-abe4-7f529d121046) **- Name:** 'Guest accounts with owner permissions on Azure resources should be removed'
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: It is good practice to use a dynamic security group to manage guest users.  To create the dynamic security group:  1. Navigate to the 'Microsoft Entra ID' blade in the Azure Portal 2. Select the 'Groups' item 3. Create new 4. Type of 'dynamic' 5. Use the following dynamic selection rule. "(user.userType -eq "Guest")" 6. Once the group has been created, select access reviews option and create a new access review with a period of monthly and send to relevant administrators for review.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default no guest users are created.

Requirements.Description: Ensure That Use of the 'User Access Administrator' Role is Restricted

Attributes.Description: The User Access Administrator role grants the ability to view all resources and manage access assignments at any subscription or management group level within the tenant. Due to its high privilege level, this role assignment should be removed immediately after completing the necessary changes at the root scope to minimize security risks.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: The User Access Administrator role provides extensive access control privileges. Unnecessary assignments heighten the risk of privilege escalation and unauthorized access. Removing the role immediately after use minimizes security exposure.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Increased administrative effort to manage and remove role assignments appropriately.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Note:** A User Access Administrator assignment at the `/` scope cannot be removed on the `Access control (IAM)` page; removing it requires elevated access.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Subscriptions`. 3. Select a subscription. 4. Select `Access control (IAM)`. 5. In the horizontal menu select `Roles`. 6. Search for `User Access Administrator`. 7. In the `Details` column select `View`. 8. In the horizontal menu select `Assignments`. 9. Select the user you wish to remove. 10. Select `Remove`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Run the following command for each user to remove:  ``` az role assignment delete --assignee <user-principal-name> --role "User Access Administrator" --scope "/" ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Run the following command for each user to remove:  ``` Remove-AzRoleAssignment -SignInName <user-principal-name> -RoleDefinitionName 'User Access Administrator' -Scope '/' ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Note:** The command-line methods check only the `/` scope, not subscription scopes, and reading that scope requires a Global Administrator with elevated access or the User Access Administrator role at `/`.  **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Subscriptions`. 3. Select a subscription. 4. Select `Access control (IAM)`. 5. In the horizontal menu select `Roles`. 6. Search for `User Access Administrator`. 7. In the `Details` column select `View`. 8. In the horizontal menu select `Assignments`. 9. Audit the list for assignments.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command:  ``` az role assignment list --role "User Access Administrator" --scope "/" ```  Ensure that the command does not return any `User Access Administrator` role assignment information.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command:  ``` Get-AzRoleAssignment -RoleDefinitionName 'User Access Administrator' -Scope '/' | Where-Object { $_.Scope -eq '/' } ```  Ensure that the command does not return any role assignments.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default the `User Access Administrator` role is not assigned.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that All 'Privileged' Role Assignments are Periodically Reviewed

Attributes.Description: Periodic review of privileged role assignments is performed to ensure that the privileged roles assigned to users are accurate and appropriate.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Privileged roles are crown jewel assets that can be used by malicious insiders, threat actors, and even through mistake to significantly damage an organization in numerous ways. These roles should be periodically reviewed to:  - identify lingering permissions assignment (e.g. an administrator has been terminated, the administrator account is being retained, but the permissions are no longer necessary and has not been properly addressed by process) - detect lateral movement through privilege escalation (e.g. an account with administrative permission has been compromised and is elevating other accounts in an attempt to circumvent detection mechanisms)
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Increased administrative effort to manage and remove role assignments appropriately.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Subscriptions`. 3. Select a subscription. 4. Select `Access control (IAM)`. 5. In the horizontal menu, select `Roles`. 6. In the second horizontal menu select `Privileged administrator roles`. 7. For each role, audit by selecting the `View` link under the `Details` column. 8. Once selected, choose `Assignments` to view the users and resources that are assigned the role.  **Note:** The judgement of what constitutes 'appropriate and current' assignments requires a clear understanding of your organization's personnel, systems, policy, and security requirements. This cannot be effectively prescribed in procedure.

Requirements.Description: Ensure Disabled User Accounts do not Have Read, Write, or Owner Permissions

Attributes.Description: When a user account is disabled, any Azure role assignments it holds (including read, write, or owner permissions) remain in place unless they are explicitly removed, leaving latent access attached to an account that is no longer in active use. Remove read, write, and owner role assignments from disabled Azure user accounts. While an automated assessment procedure exists for this recommendation, the assessment status remains manual. Removing role assignments from disabled user accounts depends on the context and requirements of each organization and environment.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Disabled accounts should not retain access to resources, as this poses a security risk. Removing role assignments mitigates potential unauthorized access and enforces the principle of least privilege.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Ensure disabled accounts are not relied on for break glass or automated processes before removing roles to avoid service disruption.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Entra ID`. 2. Under `Manage`, click `Users`. 3. Click `Add filter`. 4. Click `Account enabled`. 5. Click the toggle switch to set the value to `No`. 6. Click `Apply`. 7. Click the `Display name` of a disabled user account with read, write, or owner roles assigned. 8. Click `Azure role assignments`. 9. Click the name of a read, write, or owner role. 10. Click `Assignments`. 11. Click `Remove` in the row for the disabled user account. 12. Click `Yes`. 13. Repeat steps 7-12 for disabled user accounts requiring remediation.  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Connect to Azure, then remove each read, write, or owner role from the disabled account (repeat per role and per account):  ``` Connect-AzAccount ```  ``` $user = Get-AzADUser -UserPrincipalName "<user@domain.com>" Remove-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $user.Id -RoleDefinitionName "<role-definition-name>" ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Entra ID`. 2. Under `Manage`, click `Users`. 3. Click `Add filter`. 4. Click `Account enabled`. 5. Click the toggle switch to set the value to `No`. 6. Click `Apply`. 7. Click the `Display name` of a disabled user account. 8. Click `Azure role assignments`. 9. Ensure that no read, write, or owner roles are assigned to the user account. 10. Repeat steps 7-9 for each disabled user account.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Connect to Azure, then list the Azure role assignments held by each disabled user account:  ``` Connect-AzAccount ```  ``` # Disabled user accounts (Get-AzADUser returns the object id as .Id) $disabled = Get-AzADUser -Filter "accountEnabled eq false" ```  ``` foreach ($user in $disabled) { Get-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $user.Id | Select-Object @{Name='UserPrincipalName';Expression={$user.UserPrincipalName}}, RoleDefinitionName, Scope } ```  Ensure that no read, write, or owner roles are returned for any disabled account. An empty result for a user means it holds no Azure role assignments and is compliant.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [0cfea604-3201-4e14-88fc-fae4c427a6c5](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F0cfea604-3201-4e14-88fc-fae4c427a6c5) **- Name:** 'Blocked accounts with owner permissions on Azure resources should be removed' - **Policy ID:** [8d7e1fde-fe26-4b5f-8108-f8e432cbc2be](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F8d7e1fde-fe26-4b5f-8108-f8e432cbc2be) **- Name:** 'Blocked accounts with read and write permissions on Azure resources should be removed'
Attributes.DefaultValue: Disabled user accounts retain their prior role assignments.

Requirements.Description: Ensure 'Tenant Creator' Role Assignments are Periodically Reviewed

Attributes.Description: Perform a periodic review of the Tenant Creator role assignment to ensure that the assignments are accurate and appropriate.  This recommendation should be applied alongside the recommendation `Ensure that 'Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants' is set to 'Yes'`.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Unnecessary assignments increase the risk of privilege escalation and unauthorized access.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Verify that the Tenant Creator role is no longer required by any assignments before removal to avoid disruption of critical functions.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Entra ID`. 2. Under `Manage`, click `Roles and administrators`. 3. In the search bar, type `Tenant Creator`. 4. Click the role. 5. Click the name of an assignment. 6. Check the box next to the `Tenant Creator` role. 7. Click `X Remove assignments`. 8. Click `Yes`. 9. Repeat steps 1-8 for each assignment requiring remediation.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Entra ID`. 2. Under `Manage`, click `Roles and administrators`. 3. In the search bar, type `Tenant Creator`. 4. Click the role. 5. Review the assignments and ensure that they are appropriate.
Attributes.DefaultValue: The Tenant Creator role is not assigned by default.

Requirements.Description: Ensure All Non-privileged Role Assignments are Periodically Reviewed

Attributes.Description: Perform a periodic review of non-privileged role assignments to ensure that the non-privileged roles assigned to users are appropriate.  **Note:** Determining 'appropriate' assignments requires a clear understanding of your organization's personnel, systems, policies, and security requirements. This cannot be effectively prescribed in a procedure.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: To ensure the principle of least privilege is followed, non-privileged role assignments should be reviewed periodically to confirm that users are granted only the minimum level of permissions they need to perform their tasks.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Increased administrative effort to manage and remove role assignments appropriately.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Subscriptions`. 2. Click the name of a subscription. 3. Click `Access control (IAM)`. 4. Click `Role assignments`. 5. Click `Job function roles`. 6. Check the box next to any inappropriate assignments. 7. Click `Delete`. 8. Click `Yes`. 9. Repeat steps 1-8 for each subscription.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Subscriptions`. 2. Click the name of a subscription. 3. Click `Access control (IAM)`. 4. Click `Role assignments`. 5. Click `Job function roles`. 6. For each role, ensure the assignments are appropriate. 7. Repeat steps 1-6 for each subscription.
Attributes.DefaultValue: Users do not have non-privileged roles assigned to them by default.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that No Custom Subscription Administrator Roles Exist

Attributes.Description: The principle of least privilege should be followed and only necessary privileges should be assigned instead of allowing full administrative access.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Custom roles in Azure with administrative access can obfuscate the permissions granted and introduce complexity and blind spots to the management of privileged identities. For less mature security programs without regular identity audits, the creation of Custom roles should be avoided entirely. For more mature security programs with regular identity audits, Custom Roles should be audited for use and assignment, used minimally, and the principle of least privilege should be observed when granting permissions
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Subscriptions will need to be handled by Administrators with permissions.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Subscriptions`. 3. Select a subscription. 4. Select `Access control (IAM)`. 5. Select `Roles`. 6. Click `Type` and select `Custom role` from the drop-down menu. 7. Check the box next to each role which grants subscription administrator privileges. 8. Select `Delete`. 9. Select `Yes`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  List custom roles:  ``` az role definition list --custom-role-only True ```  Check for entries with `assignableScope` of the `subscription`, and an action of `*`.  To remove a violating role:  ``` az role definition delete --name <role name> ```  Note that any role assignments must be removed before a custom role can be deleted. Ensure impact is assessed before deleting a custom role granting subscription administrator privileges.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Subscriptions`. 3. Select a subscription. 4. Select `Access control (IAM)`. 5. Select `Roles`. 6. Click `Type` and select `Custom role` from the drop-down menu. 7. Select `View` next to a role. 8. Select `JSON`. 9. Check for `assignableScopes` set to the subscription, and `actions` set to `*`. 10. Repeat steps 7-9 for each custom role.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  List custom roles:  ``` az role definition list --custom-role-only True ```  Check for entries with `assignableScope` of the `subscription`, and an action of `*`  **Audit from PowerShell**  ``` Connect-AzAccount Get-AzRoleDefinition |Where-Object {($_.IsCustom -eq $true) -and ($_.Actions.contains('*'))} ```  Check the output for `AssignableScopes` value set to the subscription.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [a451c1ef-c6ca-483d-87ed-f49761e3ffb5](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2Fa451c1ef-c6ca-483d-87ed-f49761e3ffb5) **- Name:** 'Audit usage of custom RBAC roles'
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, no custom owner roles are created.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that a Dedicated Role is Assigned Permissions for Administering Resource Locks

Attributes.Description: Resource locks prevent deletion or modification of a subscription, resource group, or resource regardless of a user's role. A dedicated role that grants only lock permissions, either the built-in Locks Contributor role or a custom role, lets designated administrators manage locks without holding Owner or User Access Administrator.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Outside a few specialized built-in roles, only Owner and User Access Administrator can create or delete locks, and both also control role assignments. Granting either role just to manage locks lets the holder grant themselves or anyone else any access within that scope, while the built-in Locks Contributor role or an equivalent custom role grants lock management alone.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Maintaining the dedicated role's assignments, and the custom role definition if one is used, adds administrative overhead at each scope where the role is assigned.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  To use the built-in role, assign `Locks Contributor` by following steps 17-26 below, selecting `Locks Contributor` in step 19. To create a custom role instead:  1. In the Azure portal, navigate to a subscription or resource group. 2. Click `Access control (IAM)`. 3. Click `+ Add`. 4. Click `Add custom role`. 5. In the `Custom role name` field enter `Resource Lock Administrator`. 6. In the `Description` field enter `Can Administer Resource Locks`. 7. For `Baseline permissions` select `Start from scratch`. 8. Click `Next`. 9. Click `Add permissions`. 10. In the `Search for a permission` box, type `Microsoft.Authorization/locks`. 11. Click the result. 12. Check the box next to `Permission`. 13. Click `Add`. 14. Click `Review + create`. 15. Click `Create`. 16. Click `OK`. 17. Click `+ Add`. 18. Click `Add role assignment`. 19. In the `Search by role name, description, permission, or ID` box, type `Resource Lock Administrator`. 20. Select the role. 21. Click `Next`. 22. Click `+ Select members`. 23. Select appropriate members. 24. Click `Select`. 25. Click `Review + assign`. 26. Click `Review + assign` again. 27. Repeat steps 1-26 for each subscription or resource group requiring remediation.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  To use the built-in role, assign it:  ``` az role assignment create --assignee <object-id> --role "Locks Contributor" --scope <scope> ```  To create a custom role at a management group instead, then assign it:  ``` az role definition create --role-definition '{"Name":"Resource Lock Administrator","Description":"Can Administer Resource Locks","Actions":["Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*"],"AssignableScopes":["/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<management-group-name>"]}' ```  ``` az role assignment create --assignee <object-id> --role "Resource Lock Administrator" --scope <scope> ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  To use the built-in role, assign it:  ``` New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId <object-id> -RoleDefinitionName "Locks Contributor" -Scope <scope> ```  To create a custom role at a management group instead, then assign it:  ``` $role = Get-AzRoleDefinition "User Access Administrator" $role.Id = $null $role.Name = "Resource Lock Administrator" $role.Description = "Can Administer Resource Locks" $role.Actions.Clear() $role.Actions.Add("Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*") $role.AssignableScopes.Clear() # Scope the role to a management group $role.AssignableScopes.Add("/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<management-group-name>") New-AzRoleDefinition -Role $role Get-AzRoleDefinition "Resource Lock Administrator" ```  ``` New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId <object-id> -RoleDefinitionName "Resource Lock Administrator" -Scope <scope> ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. In the Azure portal, navigate to a subscription or resource group. 2. Click `Access control (IAM)`. 3. Click `Role assignments`, search for `Locks Contributor`, and review its assignments. 4. Click `Roles`, set `Type` to `Custom role`, and for each custom role click `View` in the `Details` column and review its permissions. 5. For each custom role that qualifies, click `Assignments` and review the assignments. 6. Ensure that at least one qualifying role, either `Locks Contributor` or a custom role that grants `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*` or both `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/write` and `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/delete`, is assigned to appropriate members. 7. Repeat steps 1-6 for each subscription or resource group.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  List the custom roles whose actions include a resource lock permission:  ``` az role definition list --custom-role-only true --query "[?permissions[?actions[?starts_with(@, 'Microsoft.Authorization/locks')]]].{roleName:roleName, actions:permissions[].actions, assignableScopes:assignableScopes}" --output json ```  List the assignments of the built-in role and of each qualifying custom role:  ``` az role assignment list --role "Locks Contributor" --all --include-inherited --output table ```  ``` az role assignment list --role "<custom-role-name>" --all --include-inherited --output table ```  Ensure that `Locks Contributor`, or a custom role whose actions include `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*` or both `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/write` and `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/delete`, is assigned only to appropriate members.  **Audit from PowerShell**  List the custom roles whose actions include a resource lock permission:  ``` Get-AzRoleDefinition -Custom | Where-Object { $_.Actions -like 'Microsoft.Authorization/locks*' } | Format-Table Name, Id, Actions, AssignableScopes ```  List the assignments of the built-in role and of each qualifying custom role:  ``` Get-AzRoleAssignment -RoleDefinitionName "Locks Contributor" ```  ``` Get-AzRoleAssignment -RoleDefinitionName "<custom-role-name>" ```  Ensure that `Locks Contributor`, or a custom role whose actions include `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*` or both `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/write` and `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/delete`, is assigned only to appropriate members.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: The built-in Locks Contributor role (ID `28bf596f-4eb7-45ce-b5bc-6cf482fec137`) grants only `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/read`, `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/write`, and `Microsoft.Authorization/locks/delete`, and satisfies this recommendation. A custom role is needed only when an organization wants different assignable scopes or permissions.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, the built-in Locks Contributor role exists but is not assigned, and no custom lock administration role exists.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant' and 'Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant' is set to 'Permit no one'

Attributes.Description: Users who are set as subscription owners are able to make administrative changes to the subscriptions and move them into and out of Microsoft Entra ID.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Permissions to move subscriptions in and out of a Microsoft Entra tenant must only be given to appropriate administrative personnel. A subscription that is moved into a Microsoft Entra tenant may be within a folder to which other users have elevated permissions. This prevents loss of data or unapproved changes of the objects within by potential bad actors.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Subscriptions will need to have these settings turned off to be moved.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From the Azure Portal Home select the portal menu 2. Select `Subscriptions` 3. In the horizontal menu select `Manage Policies` 4. Set `Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant` and `Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant` to `Permit no one` 5. Click `Save changes`
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From the Azure Portal Home select the portal menu 2. Select `Subscriptions` 3. In the horizontal menu select `Manage Policies` 4. Ensure `Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant` and `Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant` are set to `Permit no one`
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default `Subscription leaving Microsoft Entra tenant` and `Subscription entering Microsoft Entra tenant` are set to `Allow everyone (default)`

Requirements.Description: Ensure there are between 2 and 3 Subscription Owners

Attributes.Description: The Owner role in Azure grants full control over all resources in a subscription, including the ability to assign roles to others.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Limit the number of security principals (users, groups, service principals, and managed identities) assigned the Owner role to between 2 and 3. If groups are used, ensure their membership is tightly controlled and regularly reviewed to avoid privilege sprawl.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Implementation may require changes in administrative workflows or the redistribution of roles and responsibilities. The recommendation to have between 2 and 3 Owners per subscription must account for all security principals that can be assigned the Owner role, not just individual users. This includes:  - User accounts - Entra ID groups - Service principals (used by applications or automation) - Managed identities (system-assigned or user-assigned)
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Subscriptions`. 2. Click the name of a subscription. 3. Click `Access Controls (IAM)`. 4. Click `Role assignments`. 5. Click `Role : All`. 6. Click the arrow next to `All`. 7. Click `Owner`. 8. Check the box next to members from whom the owner role should be removed. 9. Click `Delete`. 10. Click `Yes`. 11. Repeat steps 1-10 for each subscription requiring remediation.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to delete role assignments by role assignment id:  ``` az role assignment delete --ids <role-assignment-ids> ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Subscriptions`. 2. Click the name of a subscription. 3. Click `Access Controls (IAM)`. 4. Click `Role assignments`. 5. Click `Role : All`. 6. Click the arrow next to `All`. 7. Click `Owner`. 8. Ensure a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 members are returned. 9. Repeat steps 1-8 for each subscription.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to list members with role `Owner` at a given subscription scope:  ``` az role assignment list --role Owner --scope /subscriptions/<subscription-id> --query "[].{PrincipalName:principalName, Type:principalType}" ```  Ensure a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 members are returned.  For each Owner assignment, check: If principalType == Group, review group membership. If principalType == ServicePrincipal or ManagedIdentity, validate necessity and scope.  Repeat for each subscription.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command to list members with role `Owner` at a given subscription scope:  ``` Get-AzRoleAssignment -RoleDefinitionName Owner -Scope /subscriptions/<subscription-id> ```  Ensure a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 members are returned.  Repeat for each subscription.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [09024ccc-0c5f-475e-9457-b7c0d9ed487b](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F09024ccc-0c5f-475e-9457-b7c0d9ed487b) **- Name:** 'There should be more than one owner assigned to your subscription' - **Policy ID:** [4f11b553-d42e-4e3a-89be-32ca364cad4c](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F4f11b553-d42e-4e3a-89be-32ca364cad4c) **- Name:** 'A maximum of 3 owners should be designated for your subscription'
Attributes.DefaultValue: A subscription has 1 owner by default.

Requirements.Description: Ensure the default management group for new subscriptions is not the root management group

Attributes.Description: A tenant places each new subscription under one of two scopes: the root management group, or another management group the organization designates. The `Default management group` hierarchy setting selects between them for the whole tenant.  **Prerequisites:** Create the management group that will receive new subscriptions and assign it the policies and role assignments that new subscriptions must carry.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: With the root management group as the default, a new subscription inherits only root-scope policy and role assignments, which organizations often keep minimal because they reach every resource in the tenant. Resources deployed before the subscription is moved run without the organization's guardrails, and compliance reporting scoped to child management groups does not cover them.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: The setting applies only to subscriptions created or added after the change; subscriptions already under the root management group stay there until moved. New subscriptions inherit the default management group's assignments from creation, so a policy with a `Deny` effect assigned there can block a subscription owner's first deployments.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Note:** These steps require the `Hierarchy Settings Administrator` or `Owner` role on the root management group.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Management groups`. 2. Click the root management group (displayed by default as `Tenant Root Group`). 3. Click `Settings`. 4. Click `Change default management group`. 5. Select the management group designated for new subscriptions. 6. Click `Select`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Set the default management group with `update`, or with `create` if the audit returned no hierarchy settings:  ``` az account management-group hierarchy-settings update --name <tenant-id> --default-management-group /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<management-group-id> ```  ``` az account management-group hierarchy-settings create --name <tenant-id> --default-management-group /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<management-group-id> ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Set the default management group with `Update-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting`, or with `New-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting` if the audit returned no hierarchy settings:  ``` Update-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting -GroupName <tenant-id> -DefaultManagementGroup <management-group-id> ```  ``` New-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting -GroupName <tenant-id> -DefaultManagementGroup <management-group-id> ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Note:** These steps require the `Reader` or `Hierarchy Settings Administrator` role on the root management group.  **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Management groups`. 2. Click the root management group (displayed by default as `Tenant Root Group`). 3. Click `Settings`. 4. Verify `Default management group` names a management group other than the root management group.  The setting is non-compliant when it shows the root management group.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command; the root management group ID equals the tenant ID:  ``` az account management-group hierarchy-settings list --name <tenant-id> ```  Compliant output shows `defaultManagementGroup` naming a management group other than `<tenant-id>`. An empty result or value, or the root ID, is non-compliant.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command against the root management group:  ``` Get-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting -GroupName <tenant-id> ```  Compliant output shows `DefaultManagementGroup` naming a management group other than `<tenant-id>`. An empty value or the root ID is non-compliant.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, new subscriptions are placed under the root management group.

Requirements.Description: Ensure creating management groups requires write permission on the root management group

Attributes.Description: A tenant permits management group creation under one of two rules: any user or service principal in the tenant, or only principals granted management group write permission on the root management group. The `Require write permissions for creating new management groups` setting selects between them.  **Prerequisites:** Grant management group write permission on the root management group to every user and pipeline identity that must continue to create management groups.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: With the setting off, any user or service principal in the tenant can create a management group under the root or default management group and receives the `Owner` role on it. A compromised low-privilege account thereby gains a persistent privileged scope in the hierarchy, holding `Owner` over any subscription later placed in that management group.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: The setting governs only creation; it does not remove existing management groups or the `Owner` assignments their creators received, so management groups created while it was off keep those owners until someone reviews them.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Note:** These steps require the `Hierarchy Settings Administrator` or `Owner` role on the root management group.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Management groups`. 2. Click the root management group (displayed by default as `Tenant Root Group`). 3. Click `Settings`. 4. Enable `Require write permissions for creating new management groups`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Require authorization with `update`, or with `create` if the audit returned no hierarchy settings:  ``` az account management-group hierarchy-settings update --name <tenant-id> --require-authorization-for-group-creation true ```  ``` az account management-group hierarchy-settings create --name <tenant-id> --require-authorization-for-group-creation true ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Require authorization with `Update-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting`, or with `New-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting` if the audit returned no hierarchy settings:  ``` Update-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting -GroupName <tenant-id> -Authorization $true ```  ``` New-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting -GroupName <tenant-id> -Authorization $true ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Note:** These steps require the `Reader` or `Hierarchy Settings Administrator` role on the root management group.  **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Management groups`. 2. Click the root management group (displayed by default as `Tenant Root Group`). 3. Click `Settings`. 4. Verify `Require write permissions for creating new management groups` is enabled.  The setting is non-compliant when the toggle is off.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command; the root management group ID equals the tenant ID:  ``` az account management-group hierarchy-settings list --name <tenant-id> ```  Compliant output shows `requireAuthorizationForGroupCreation` set to `true`. An empty result, a missing value, or `false` is non-compliant.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command against the root management group:  ``` Get-AzManagementGroupHierarchySetting -GroupName <tenant-id> ```  Compliant output shows `RequireAuthorizationForGroupCreation` set to `true`. An empty value or `false` is non-compliant.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Management group write permission on the root management group is included in the `Owner`, `Contributor` and `Management Group Contributor` roles when they are assigned at that scope.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, the setting is off and any user or service principal in the tenant can create a management group.

Requirements.Description: Ensure Emergency Access Accounts Can Regain Azure Resource Access

Attributes.Description: Microsoft Entra ID roles grant no Azure RBAC, so a tenant can lose all ability to manage its subscriptions while Global Administrators remain. A Global Administrator restores access by setting `Access management for Azure resources` to `Yes`, which grants root-scope access. Maintain emergency access accounts (aka "break-glass accounts") and a tested recovery procedure.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Because Entra ID and Azure RBAC are secured separately, a tenant can reach a state where no account holds Owner or User Access Administrator at any scope, after the last privileged account leaves or root-scope access is removed for least privilege. If no Global Administrator can sign in, no one can elevate access, and recovery depends on Microsoft support.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Emergency access accounts are highly privileged standing credentials, so their sign-ins must raise alerts to keep them from becoming an unguarded entry point. Each recovery and test temporarily grants control over every subscription at the root scope, so it must end by removing that elevation. Conditional Access exclusion applies only where Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher is licensed.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Create at least two cloud-only emergency access accounts (not synchronized from on-premises) and assign them the Global Administrator role as an active, permanent assignment (not PIM-eligible), following Microsoft's emergency access account guidance, and store their credentials under dual control. 2. Configure monitoring so that every sign-in by an emergency access account raises a high-priority alert. 3. Exclude the emergency access accounts (for example through a dedicated group) from every Conditional Access policy that blocks or restricts sign-in; report-only policies need no exclusion. 4. Document the recovery procedure. During a recovery, an emergency access account signs in, goes to `Microsoft Entra ID` > `Manage` > `Properties`, sets `Access management for Azure resources` to `Yes`, then signs out and back in. It assigns `Owner` at the specific subscription or management group being recovered — never the Tenant Root Group — to the account that will own it, restores normal access, then sets `Access management for Azure resources` back to `No` (removing the root-scope `User Access Administrator` assignment) and signs out. 5. Test the procedure at least every 90 days and record each result.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  An emergency access account elevates access, then signs out and back in. It assigns `Owner` at the subscription or management group being recovered (never the Tenant Root Group), then removes the elevation afterward:  ``` az rest --method post --url "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/elevateAccess?api-version=2016-07-01" az role assignment create --assignee "<recovery-owner-object-id>" --role "Owner" --scope "/subscriptions/<subscription-id>" az role assignment delete --assignee "<emergency-account-object-id>" --role "User Access Administrator" --scope "/" ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  After the emergency access account elevates access in the portal and signs out and back in, it assigns `Owner` at the subscription or management group being recovered (never the Tenant Root Group), then removes the elevation:  ``` New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId "<recovery-owner-object-id>" -RoleDefinitionName "Owner" -Scope "/subscriptions/<subscription-id>" Remove-AzRoleAssignment -SignInName "<emergency-account-upn>" -RoleDefinitionName "User Access Administrator" -Scope "/" ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Note:** Enumerating Azure role assignments at the root scope (`/`) requires read access there — a Global Administrator can read elevated-access assignments, or the auditor elevates access to enumerate them and removes that elevation afterward, discounting their own temporary `User Access Administrator` assignment at `/` from the results.  **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to `Users` and confirm at least two dedicated emergency access accounts exist that are cloud-only (on-premises sync not enabled), not assigned to named individuals, and hold the Global Administrator role as an active, permanent assignment (not PIM-eligible). 2. Open the recovery runbook and confirm it documents the elevate-access recovery and records a successful test within the last 90 days. 3. Confirm an alert rule is configured to fire on any sign-in by each emergency access account. 4. In the Azure portal, go to `Management groups`, select the Tenant Root Group, then `Access control (IAM)` > `Role assignments`, and confirm no emergency access account holds a standing `Owner` or `User Access Administrator` assignment. Within the retained (or exported) log period, confirm each past elevate-access entry was followed by its removal — in `Microsoft Entra ID` > `Monitoring` > `Audit logs` (Service filter `Azure RBAC (Elevated Access)`, currently in preview) or in `Monitor` > `Activity log` with `Activity` set to `Directory Activity` (operation `Assigns the caller to User Access Administrator role`). 5. For each Conditional Access policy that blocks or restricts sign-in, confirm the emergency access accounts are excluded (for example through a dedicated group); report-only policies need no exclusion.  The recommendation passes when at least two cloud-only emergency access accounts with active, permanent Global Administrator assignments and a runbook tested within 90 days are present, sign-in alerting is configured for each account, each account is excluded from the Conditional Access policies that block or restrict sign-in, and no emergency access account holds a standing `Owner` or `User Access Administrator` assignment at the root scope (`/`) or the Tenant Root Group, discounting any temporary elevation held by the auditor.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  List any standing privileged assignments at the root scope and the Tenant Root Group management group (its ID equals the tenant ID):  ``` az role assignment list --scope "/" --query "[?roleDefinitionName=='Owner' || roleDefinitionName=='User Access Administrator'].{principal:principalName, role:roleDefinitionName, scope:scope}" --output table az role assignment list --scope "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<tenant-root-group-id>" --query "[?roleDefinitionName=='Owner' || roleDefinitionName=='User Access Administrator'].{principal:principalName, role:roleDefinitionName, scope:scope}" --output table ```  Neither command should list an emergency access account; disregard the auditor's own temporary `User Access Administrator` entry at `/`.  **Audit from PowerShell**  List any standing privileged assignments at the root scope and the Tenant Root Group management group:  ``` Get-AzRoleAssignment -Scope "/" | Where-Object { $_.RoleDefinitionName -in "Owner", "User Access Administrator" } Get-AzRoleAssignment -Scope "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/<tenant-root-group-id>" | Where-Object { $_.RoleDefinitionName -in "Owner", "User Access Administrator" } ```  Neither list should include an emergency access account; disregard the auditor's own temporary `User Access Administrator` entry at `/`.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Microsoft Entra ID roles and Azure RBAC are governed separately, so Global Administrator rights cannot assign Azure roles until access is elevated; elevation grants `User Access Administrator` at the root scope and must be removed afterward. Recovery grants `Owner` only at the affected subscription or management group, never the Tenant Root Group (whose ID equals the tenant ID). Cloud-only accounts have `onPremisesSyncEnabled` not set to true. No built-in Azure Policy evaluates root-scope assignments or emergency access, so this control is assessed as Manual and the scriptable check confirms only the absence of standing root-scope privilege.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, a tenant has no emergency access accounts and no recovery procedure, and only a Global Administrator can elevate access to the root scope.

Requirements.Description: Ensure Service Principals Holding Azure Role Assignments Do Not Use Client Secrets

Attributes.Description: A service principal that holds an Azure role assignment signs in with a client secret, a certificate, or a federated credential, unless it is a managed identity, which has no readable credential.  **Prerequisites:** Move each workload that signs in with a client secret to a managed identity, a federated credential, or a certificate, and confirm it works before removing the secret.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: A client secret is a long-lived string that the workload sends to Microsoft Entra ID, so anyone who copies it from code, configuration, or a pipeline can sign in as the application from anywhere. The holder inherits every Azure role the service principal holds until the secret expires or is removed, and the sign-ins look like the workload's own.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Each workload that signs in with a client secret must be re-credentialed and redeployed, and certificates add issuance, storage, and rotation work. Some third-party products and integrations accept only a client secret, so this recommendation may impact the utility of those tools or require replacing them.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: Complete the prerequisites in the Description before remediating.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Microsoft Entra ID` > `App registrations` > `All applications`. 2. Select an application that the audit identified. 3. Click `Certificates & secrets`. 4. Click `Client secrets`. 5. Click `Delete` next to each client secret. 6. Click `Yes`. 7. Repeat steps 2-6 for each application the audit identified.  Remove client secrets held directly on a service principal from Azure CLI or PowerShell.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Remove each application client secret, using the key ID the audit listed:  ``` az ad app credential delete --id <app-id> --key-id <key-id> ```  List the client secrets held directly on a service principal, then remove each one:  ``` az ad sp credential list --id <service-principal-object-id> --output table ```  ``` az ad sp credential delete --id <service-principal-object-id> --key-id <key-id> ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  List the application's client secrets, then remove each one:  ``` (Get-AzADApplication -ApplicationId <app-id>).PasswordCredentials | Select-Object KeyId, DisplayName, EndDateTime ```  ``` Remove-AzADAppCredential -ApplicationId <app-id> -KeyId <key-id> ```  List the client secrets held directly on a service principal, then remove each one:  ``` (Get-AzADServicePrincipal -ObjectId <service-principal-object-id>).PasswordCredentials | Select-Object KeyId, DisplayName, EndDateTime ```  ``` Remove-AzADSpCredential -ObjectId <service-principal-object-id> -KeyId <key-id> ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Note:** These steps require read access to role assignments in each subscription and to applications and service principals in Microsoft Entra ID.  **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Subscriptions`. 2. Select a subscription. 3. Click `Access control (IAM)`. 4. Click `Role assignments`. 5. Click `Type : All`. 6. Select `Apps`. 7. Record the name of each service principal listed. 8. Repeat steps 1-7 for each subscription. 9. Navigate to `Microsoft Entra ID` > `App registrations` > `All applications`. 10. Select an application recorded in step 7. 11. Click `Certificates & secrets`. 12. Click `Client secrets`. 13. Verify that no client secret is listed. 14. Repeat steps 10-13 for each recorded application.  The portal does not show client secrets on a service principal. Managed identities have no `App registrations` entry and are compliant; audit service principals and applications from other tenants from Azure CLI or PowerShell.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Per subscription, list each role-holding service principal with its type, owning tenant, and secret count:  ``` for id in $(az role assignment list --all --include-inherited --query "[?principalType=='ServicePrincipal'].principalId" --output tsv | sort -u); do az ad sp show --id "$id" --query "{name:displayName, type:servicePrincipalType, appId:appId, appTenant:appOwnerOrganizationId, spSecrets:length(passwordCredentials)}" --output table done ```  For each `Application` row whose `appTenant` is your tenant, list its client secrets:  ``` az ad app credential list --id <app-id> --output table ```  Compliant: every `spSecrets` is `0` and each list is empty; any secret is non-compliant.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Per subscription, list each role-holding service principal with its type and secret counts:  ``` $tenantId = (Get-AzContext).Tenant.Id Get-AzRoleAssignment | Where-Object ObjectType -eq 'ServicePrincipal' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty ObjectId -Unique | ForEach-Object { $sp = Get-AzADServicePrincipal -ObjectId $_ $appSecrets = if ($sp.ServicePrincipalType -eq 'Application' -and $sp.AppOwnerOrganizationId -eq $tenantId) { @((Get-AzADApplication -ApplicationId $sp.AppId).PasswordCredentials).Count } else { 'n/a' } [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $sp.DisplayName; Type = $sp.ServicePrincipalType; SpSecrets = @($sp.PasswordCredentials).Count; AppSecrets = $appSecrets } } ```  Compliant: every `SpSecrets` value is `0` and every `AppSecrets` value is `0` or `n/a`. Any other value is non-compliant.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Microsoft Entra application management policies can block new client secrets tenant-wide through `Block password addition` under `Enterprise apps` > `Application policies` in the Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft lists them as available without a Workload ID Premium license; they do not remove existing secrets. For a multitenant application registered in another tenant, only credentials on the local service principal are visible, and the publisher manages the application's own credentials. No built-in Azure Policy evaluates Microsoft Entra application credentials.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, a new app registration has no credentials.

Requirements.Description: Ensure Role Assignment Management is Delegated with the 'Role Based Access Control Administrator' Role and Conditions

Attributes.Description: Role assignment management is delegated through `User Access Administrator`, or through `Role Based Access Control Administrator` with or without a role assignment condition that limits the roles and principals the delegate can assign. Root-scope assignments are covered by 'Ensure That Use of the 'User Access Administrator' Role is Restricted'.  **Prerequisites:** Identify the roles and principal types each delegate assigns, including automation pipelines, so the condition does not block required assignments.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: User Access Administrator and an unconstrained Role Based Access Control Administrator let the holder assign any role, including Owner, to any principal at their scope, themselves included. A compromised or careless delegate can therefore take full control of every resource in that scope and hand assignment rights to others, with no limit short of removing the assignment.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Each delegate needs a condition naming the roles, and optionally the principals, it may assign; automation that assigns roles fails outside its condition. Policy assignments whose deployIfNotExists definitions need `User Access Administrator`, such as 'Configure selected Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans with managed extensions', hold it through a managed identity, and removing it stops their remediation.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: Complete the prerequisites in the Description before remediating.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Subscriptions`. 2. Select a subscription. 3. Click `Access control (IAM)`. 4. Click `Role assignments`. 5. Check the box next to each assignment the audit identified. 6. Click `Delete`. 7. Click `Yes`. 8. Click `+ Add`. 9. Click `Add role assignment`. 10. Click `Privileged administrator roles`. 11. Select `Role Based Access Control Administrator`. 12. Click `Next`. 13. Click `+ Select members`. 14. Select the delegate. 15. Click `Select`. 16. Click `Next`. 17. Under `What user can do`, select `Allow user to only assign selected roles to selected principals (fewer privileges)`. 18. Click `Select roles and principals`. 19. Click `Configure` on the condition template that fits the delegation, such as `Constrain roles`. 20. Select the roles, and the principal types or principals, the delegate may assign. 21. Click `Save`. 22. Click `Review + assign`. 23. Repeat steps 1-22 for each delegate and subscription.  Remove an assignment inherited from a management group at the management group scope, using Azure CLI or PowerShell.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Save the condition to `condition.txt`; this example limits the delegate to assigning and removing the listed roles:  ``` ((!(ActionMatches{'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'})) OR (@Request[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:RoleDefinitionId] ForAnyOfAnyValues:GuidEquals {<role-definition-id>})) AND ((!(ActionMatches{'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/delete'})) OR (@Resource[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:RoleDefinitionId] ForAnyOfAnyValues:GuidEquals {<role-definition-id>})) ```  Remove each assignment the audit returned:  ``` az role assignment delete --ids <role-assignment-id> ```  Assign the constrained role, where `<principal-type>` is `User`, `Group`, or `ServicePrincipal`:  ``` condition=$(cat condition.txt) az role assignment create --assignee-object-id <object-id> --assignee-principal-type <principal-type> --role "Role Based Access Control Administrator" --scope <scope> --condition "$condition" --condition-version "2.0" ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Remove each assignment the audit returned:  ``` Remove-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId <object-id> -RoleDefinitionName "<role-name>" -Scope <scope> ```  Assign the constrained role with the condition saved in `condition.txt`:  ``` New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId <object-id> -RoleDefinitionName "Role Based Access Control Administrator" -Scope <scope> -Condition (Get-Content -Path condition.txt -Raw) -ConditionVersion "2.0" ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Subscriptions`. 2. Select a subscription. 3. Click `Access control (IAM)`. 4. Click `Role assignments`. 5. Click `Privileged`. 6. Verify that no `User Access Administrator` assignment with scope `This resource` is listed. 7. Verify that each `Role Based Access Control Administrator` assignment with scope `This resource` shows `View/Edit` in the `Condition` column. 8. Repeat steps 1-7 for each subscription.  The portal cannot show a condition on an assignment inherited from a management group; audit management group, resource group, and resource scopes from Azure CLI or PowerShell.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  For each subscription, list `User Access Administrator` assignments and unconditioned `Role Based Access Control Administrator` assignments below the root scope:  ``` az role assignment list --all --include-inherited --query "[?scope!='/' && (roleDefinitionName=='User Access Administrator' || (roleDefinitionName=='Role Based Access Control Administrator' && condition==null))].{principal:principalName, type:principalType, role:roleDefinitionName, scope:scope, id:id}" --output table ```  A compliant result returns no rows. Any row is non-compliant.  **Audit from PowerShell**  For each subscription, list the same assignments:  ``` Get-AzRoleAssignment | Where-Object { $_.Scope -ne '/' -and ($_.RoleDefinitionName -eq 'User Access Administrator' -or ($_.RoleDefinitionName -eq 'Role Based Access Control Administrator' -and -not $_.Condition)) } | Select-Object DisplayName, ObjectType, RoleDefinitionName, Scope, RoleAssignmentId ```  A compliant result returns no output. Any output is non-compliant.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: `Owner` also grants role assignment rights; Owner assignments are bounded by 'Ensure there are between 2 and 3 Subscription Owners', and Microsoft recommends a condition on them as well. A delegate's condition should not allow assigning `Owner`, `User Access Administrator`, or `Role Based Access Control Administrator`. No built-in Azure Policy audits role assignment conditions; 'Azure role assignment management should be restricted to Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management' evaluates new assignment requests only. Delegation with conditions is included in every Azure subscription at no cost.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, no `User Access Administrator` or `Role Based Access Control Administrator` assignment exists below the root scope.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that a 'Diagnostic Setting' Exists for Subscription Activity Logs

Attributes.Description: A subscription's activity log is exported only when the subscription has a diagnostic setting that sends it to a Log Analytics workspace, storage account, event hub, or partner solution. Diagnostic settings for individual resources are covered by the recommendation `Ensure that Azure Monitor Resource Logging is Enabled for All Services that Support it`.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: The activity log records every control-plane operation in a subscription, including resource deletions, role assignments, and policy changes. Azure keeps these entries for only 90 days and outside any central store, so without an export to a workspace, storage account, or event hub, where retention is set, an intrusion found later cannot be reconstructed or correlated with other logs.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: The destination bills for the exported data: ingestion and retention charges apply in a Log Analytics workspace, and storage or throughput charges apply to a storage account or event hub.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Monitor`. 2. Click `Activity log`. 3. Click `Export Activity Logs`. 4. Select a subscription. 5. Click `+ Add diagnostic setting`. 6. Enter a `Diagnostic setting name`. 7. Under `Categories`, select the log categories to export. 8. Under `Destination details`, select one or more destinations: `Send to Log Analytics workspace`, `Archive to a storage account`, `Stream to an event hub`, or `Send to partner solution`. 9. Click `Save`. 10. Repeat steps 4-9 for each subscription.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Run the following command for each subscription:  ``` az monitor diagnostic-settings subscription create --subscription <subscription-id> --name <diagnostic-setting-name> --location <location> --workspace <log-analytics-workspace-resource-id> --logs '[{"category":"Administrative","enabled":true},{"category":"Security","enabled":true},{"category":"ServiceHealth","enabled":true},{"category":"Alert","enabled":true},{"category":"Recommendation","enabled":true},{"category":"Policy","enabled":true},{"category":"Autoscale","enabled":true},{"category":"ResourceHealth","enabled":true}]' ```  To send the log to a storage account or event hub instead of, or in addition to, a workspace, add `--storage-account <storage-account-resource-id>` or `--event-hub-auth-rule <event-hub-authorization-rule-id>` with `--event-hub-name <event-hub-name>`.  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Run the following commands for each subscription:  ``` $logCategories = @() foreach ($category in 'Administrative','Security','ServiceHealth','Alert','Recommendation','Policy','Autoscale','ResourceHealth') { $logCategories += New-AzDiagnosticSettingSubscriptionLogSettingsObject -Category $category -Enabled $true } New-AzSubscriptionDiagnosticSetting -SubscriptionId <subscription-id> -Name <diagnostic-setting-name> -WorkspaceId <log-analytics-workspace-resource-id> -Log $logCategories ```  To send the log to a storage account or event hub, add `-StorageAccountId <storage-account-resource-id>` or `-EventHubAuthorizationRuleId <event-hub-authorization-rule-id>` with `-EventHubName <event-hub-name>`.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Monitor`. 2. Click `Activity log`. 3. Click `Export Activity Logs`. 4. Select a subscription. 5. Ensure that at least one diagnostic setting is listed, and that it has at least one destination and at least one enabled log category. 6.
