Repeat steps 1-5 for each virtual network and subnet.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  List the default outbound access setting and delegations of every subnet:  ``` az network vnet list --query "[].{resourceGroup:resourceGroup, virtualNetwork:name, subnets:subnets[?name!='GatewaySubnet' && name!='AzureFirewallSubnet' && name!='AzureFirewallManagementSubnet' && name!='RouteServerSubnet' && name!='AzureBastionSubnet'].{subnet:name, delegations:delegations[].serviceName, defaultOutboundAccess:defaultOutboundAccess}}" --output json ```  Ensure `defaultOutboundAccess` is `false` for every listed subnet with an empty `delegations` list; `true` or `null` is non-compliant.  **Audit from PowerShell**  List the default outbound access setting of every subnet that is not delegated or dedicated to an Azure service:  ``` $excluded = 'GatewaySubnet', 'AzureFirewallSubnet', 'AzureFirewallManagementSubnet', 'RouteServerSubnet', 'AzureBastionSubnet' Get-AzVirtualNetwork | ForEach-Object { $vnet = $_ $vnet.Subnets | Where-Object { ($_.Name -notin $excluded) -and (-not $_.Delegations) } | Select-Object @{n='VirtualNetwork'; e={$vnet.Name}}, @{n='ResourceGroup'; e={$vnet.ResourceGroupName}}, Name, DefaultOutboundAccess } ```  Ensure `DefaultOutboundAccess` is `False` for every listed subnet; `True` or an empty value is non-compliant.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [7bca8353-aa3b-429b-904a-9229c4385837](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F7bca8353-aa3b-429b-904a-9229c4385837) **- Name:** 'Subnets should be private'  This Policy also evaluates delegated subnets and subnets dedicated to an Azure service, and it flags a virtual network when any of its subnets is not private, so confirm each result with the Azure Portal, Azure CLI, or PowerShell method.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Existing virtual machines keep their default outbound IP address until they are stopped and deallocated after the subnet becomes private. The Azure Advisor recommendation 'Add explicit outbound method to disable default outbound' lists the network interfaces that still have one. Microsoft states that private subnets do not apply to delegated or managed subnets that host platform services, whose outbound connectivity the service manages.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, new virtual networks get private subnets in the Azure portal and in API versions released after March 31, 2026; earlier API versions allow default outbound access.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that Network Security Group Flow Log Retention Days is Set to Greater than or equal to 90 (LEGACY)

Attributes.Description: Network security group (NSG) flow logs record IP traffic that passes through an NSG to a storage account. Each flow log's `Retention days` setting is `0`, which keeps records indefinitely, or a number of days after which records are deleted.  **Warning:** NSG flow logs retire on September 30, 2027, and new NSG flow logs cannot be created after June 30, 2025; migrate to virtual network flow logs and apply the recommendation `Ensure that Virtual Network Flow Log Retention Days is Set to Greater than or Equal to 90`.  **Note:** This recommendation applies only to NSG flow logs still in use; an NSG flow log left disabled by migration to virtual network flow logs is out of scope and should be deleted, not re-enabled.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Flow log records are the evidence used to reconstruct network connections during an investigation, and an intrusion can go undetected for weeks. With a short retention period, the records of an attacker's connections are deleted before anyone looks for them, leaving no network trail of entry or lateral movement.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Retaining flow log records for 90 days or longer increases storage consumption and cost in the destination storage account. After September 30, 2027, Azure deletes NSG flow log resources, but records already written to storage remain and follow their configured retention policy.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Network Watcher`. 2. Under `Logs`, select `Flow logs`. 3. Click the name of a network security group flow log requiring remediation. 4. If the flow log was left disabled by migration to virtual network flow logs, click `Delete` and confirm, then skip to the next flow log. 5. Set `Status` to `On`. 6. Set `Retention days` to `0` or to `90` or more. 7. Click `Save`. 8. Repeat steps 1-7 for each network security group flow log requiring remediation.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  For each network security group flow log still in use, run the following command, setting `--retention` to `0` or to `90` or more:  ``` az network watcher flow-log update --location <location> --name <flow-log-name> --enabled true --retention <number-of-days> ```  For each flow log left disabled by migration to virtual network flow logs, delete it instead:  ``` az network watcher flow-log delete --location <location> --name <flow-log-name> ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Network Watcher`. 2. Under `Logs`, select `Flow logs`. 3. Click the name of a network security group flow log that has not been replaced by a virtual network flow log. 4. Verify that `Status` is set to `On`. 5. Verify that `Retention days` is set to `0` or to `90` or more. A value of `0` retains logs indefinitely. 6. Repeat steps 1-5 for each network security group flow log still in use.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to list the regions that have a network watcher:  ``` az network watcher list --query "[].location" --output tsv ```  For each region, run the following command to list its flow logs:  ``` az network watcher flow-log list --location <location> --query "[].{name:name, target:targetResourceId, enabled:enabled, retentionDays:retentionPolicy.days}" ```  For each flow log whose `target` is a network security group still in use, verify that `enabled` is `true` and `retentionDays` is `0` or `90` or more. Disabled flow logs left by migration are out of scope.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, a network security group has no flow log.

Requirements.Description: Ensure Microsoft Defender CSPM is Set to 'On'

Attributes.Description: Enable Microsoft Defender CSPM to continuously assess cloud resources for security misconfigurations, compliance risks, and exposure to threats.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Microsoft Defender CSPM provides detailed visibility into the security state of assets and workloads and offers hardening guidance to help improve security posture.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Enabling Microsoft Defender CSPM incurs hourly charges for each billable compute, database, and storage resource. This can lead to significant costs in larger environments. Careful planning and cost analysis are recommended before enabling the service. Refer to https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/defender-for-cloud/#pricing for pricing information.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment settings`. 3. Click the name of a subscription. 4. Select the `Defender plans` blade. 5. Under `Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)`, in the row for `Defender CSPM`, set the toggle switch for `Status` to `On`. 6. Click `Save`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to enable Defender CSPM:  ``` az security pricing create --name CloudPosture --tier Standard --extensions name=ApiPosture isEnabled=true ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Run the following command to enable Defender CSPM:  ``` Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name CloudPosture -PricingTier Standard -Extension '[{"name":"ApiPosture","isEnabled":"True"}]' ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment settings`. 3. Click the name of a subscription. 4. Select the `Defender plans` blade. 5. Under `Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)`, in the row for `Defender CSPM`, ensure `Status` is set to `On`.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to get the `CloudPosture` plan pricing tier:  ``` az security pricing show --name CloudPosture --query pricingTier ```  Ensure `"Standard"` is returned.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command to get the `CloudPosture` plan pricing tier:  ``` Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name CloudPosture | Select-Object PricingTier ```  Ensure `Standard` is returned.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [1f90fc71-a595-4066-8974-d4d0802e8ef0](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F1f90fc71-a595-4066-8974-d4d0802e8ef0) **- Name:** 'Microsoft Defender CSPM should be enabled'
Attributes.DefaultValue: Defender CSPM is disabled by default.

Requirements.Description: Ensure Microsoft Defender for APIs is Set to 'On'

Attributes.Description: Microsoft Defender for APIs offers full lifecycle protection, detection, and response coverage for APIs.  While an automated assessment procedure exists for this recommendation, the assessment status remains manual. Due to its potentially high cost, Microsoft Defender for APIs may not be suitable for all environments and should be evaluated carefully before implementation.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Microsoft Defender for APIs helps provide visibility into business-critical APIs, assess and improve their security posture, prioritize vulnerability remediation, and detect threats in real time.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Microsoft Defender for APIs uses a tiered pricing model, billed per subscription per hour, with each tier allowing a set limit of API calls. In high-traffic environments, this may result in significant or prohibitive costs. Careful evaluation of API usage patterns and pricing tiers is essential before enabling the service. Refer to https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/defender-for-cloud/#pricing for pricing information.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment settings`. 3. Click the name of a subscription. 4. Select the `Defender plans` blade. 5. Under `Cloud Workload Protection (CWP)`, in the row for `APIs`, set the toggle switch for `Status` to `On`. 6. Select a plan. 7. Click `Save` to save the plan selection. 8. Click `Save` to enable Defender for APIs.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to enable Defender for APIs:  ``` az security pricing create --name Api --tier Standard --subplan <subplan> ```  Valid subplan values: `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P4`, and `P5`.  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Run the following command to enable Defender for APIs:  ``` Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name Api -PricingTier Standard -SubPlan <subplan> ```  Valid SubPlan values: `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P4`, and `P5`.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment settings`. 3. Click the name of a subscription. 4. Select the `Defender plans` blade. 5. Under `Cloud Workload Protection (CWP)`, in the row for `APIs`, ensure the `Status` is set to `On`.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to get the `Api` plan pricing tier:  ``` az security pricing show --name Api --query pricingTier ```  Ensure `"Standard"` is returned.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command to get the `Api` plan pricing tier:  ``` Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name Api | Select-Object PricingTier ```  Ensure `Standard` is returned.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [7926a6d1-b268-4586-8197-e8ae90c877d7](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F7926a6d1-b268-4586-8197-e8ae90c877d7) **- Name:** 'Microsoft Defender for APIs should be enabled'
Attributes.DefaultValue: Defender for APIs is disabled by default.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that Defender for Servers is Set to 'On'

Attributes.Description: Defender for Servers is a Microsoft Defender for Cloud plan that protects Azure and non-Azure machines. Its `Status` is `On` or `Off`; when `On`, the subplan is `Plan 1`, which provides the Defender for Endpoint integration, or `Plan 2`, which adds agentless scanning, file integrity monitoring, and just-in-time VM access.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Without the plan, machines have no Defender for Cloud threat detection and no endpoint detection and response through the Defender for Endpoint integration. An attacker who reaches a VM can then run malware, move laterally, or exploit an unpatched service without raising a Defender for Cloud alert.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Defender for Servers is billed per protected machine, and Plan 2 costs more than Plan 1; see https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/defender-for-cloud/ to estimate costs. Plan 1 can be enabled per subscription or per machine, while Plan 2 can be enabled only per subscription.  **Note:** This recommendation passes on either subplan, but in this benchmark `Ensure that 'File Integrity Monitoring' Component Status is Set to 'On'` and `Ensure that Microsoft Defender for Cloud is Configured to Check VM Operating Systems for Updates` depend on Plan 2, and `Ensure that 'Agentless scanning for machines' Component Status is Set to 'On'` depends on Plan 2 or Defender CSPM.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, select `Environment settings`. 3. Click on a subscription name. 4. Click `Defender plans` in the left pane. 5. Under `Cloud Workload Protection (CWP)`, locate `Servers` in the `Plan` column and set `Status` to `On`. 6. Select `Save`. 7. Repeat steps 1-6 for each subscription requiring remediation.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Run the following command, setting `--subplan` to `P2` where any Plan 2 recommendation in this benchmark applies:  ``` az security pricing create --name VirtualMachines --tier Standard --subplan <P1-or-P2> ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Run the following command, setting `-SubPlan` to `P2` where any Plan 2 recommendation in this benchmark applies:  ``` Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'VirtualMachines' -PricingTier 'Standard' -SubPlan '<P1-or-P2>' ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, select `Environment settings`. 3. Click on a subscription name. 4. Select `Defender plans` in the left pane. 5. Under `Cloud Workload Protection (CWP)`, locate `Servers` in the `Plan` column and verify that `Status` is set to `On`. 6. Repeat steps 1-5 for each subscription.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command for each subscription:  ``` az security pricing show --name VirtualMachines --subscription <subscription-id> --query "{tier:pricingTier, subPlan:subPlan}" ```  Verify that `tier` is `Standard`. The `subPlan` value, `P1` or `P2`, shows which plan is active.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command for each subscription:  ``` Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'VirtualMachines' | Select-Object Name, PricingTier, SubPlan ```  Verify that `PricingTier` is `Standard`. The `SubPlan` value, `P1` or `P2`, shows which plan is active.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [4da35fc9-c9e7-4960-aec9-797fe7d9051d](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F4da35fc9-c9e7-4960-aec9-797fe7d9051d) **- Name:** 'Azure Defender for servers should be enabled'
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, the Defender for Servers plan is `Off`.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Endpoint protection' Component Status is set to 'On'

Attributes.Description: The Endpoint protection component enables Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (formerly 'Advanced Threat Protection' or 'ATP' or 'WDATP' - see additional info) to communicate with Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  **Important:** When enabling integration between DfE & DfC it needs to be taken into account that this will have some side effects that may be undesirable.  1. For server 2019 & above if defender is installed (default for these server SKUs) this will trigger a deployment of the new unified agent and link to any of the extended configuration in the Defender portal. 2. If the new unified agent is required for server SKUs of Win 2016 or Linux and lower there is additional integration that needs to be switched on and agents need to be aligned.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration brings comprehensive Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) capabilities within Microsoft Defender for Cloud. This integration helps to spot abnormalities, as well as detect and respond to advanced attacks on endpoints monitored by Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  MDE works only with Standard Tier subscriptions.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Endpoint protection requires licensing and is included in these plans:  - Defender for Servers plan 1 - Defender for Servers plan 2
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment Settings`. 4. Click on the subscription name. 5. Click `Settings & monitoring`. 6. Set the `Status` for `Endpoint protection` to `On`. 7. Click `Continue`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Use the below command to enable Standard pricing tier for Storage Accounts  ``` az account get-access-token --query "{subscription:subscription,accessToken:accessToken}" --out tsv | xargs -L1 bash -c 'curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<subscriptionID>/providers/Microsoft.Security/settings/WDATP?api-version=2022-05-01 -d@"input.json"' ```  Where input.json contains the Request body json data as mentioned below.  ``` { "id": "/subscriptions/<Your_Subscription_Id>/providers/Microsoft.Security/settings/WDATP", "kind": "DataExportSettings", "type": "Microsoft.Security/settings", "properties": { "enabled": true } } ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment Settings`. 4. Click on the subscription name. 5. Click `Settings & monitoring`. 6. Ensure the `Status` for `Endpoint protection` is set to `On`.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Ensure the output of the below command is `True`  ``` az account get-access-token --query "{subscription:subscription,accessToken:accessToken}" --out tsv | xargs -L1 bash -c 'curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<subscriptionID>/providers/Microsoft.Security/settings?api-version=2022-05-01' | jq '.|.value[] | select(.name=="WDATP")'|jq '.properties.enabled' ```  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following commands to login and audit this check  ``` Connect-AzAccount Set-AzContext -Subscription <subscriptionID> Get-AzSecuritySetting | Select-Object name,enabled |where-object {$_.name -eq "WDATP"} ```  PowerShell Output - Non-Compliant  ``` Name  Enabled ----  ------- WDATP    False ```  PowerShell Output - Compliant  ``` Name  Enabled ----  ------- WDATP    True ```
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: **Important:** When enabling integration between DfE & DfC it needs to be taken into account that this will have some side effects that may be undesirable.  1. For server 2019 & above if defender is installed (default for these server SKUs) this will trigger a deployment of the new unified agent and link to any of the extended configuration in the Defender portal. 2. If the new unified agent is required for server SKUs of Win 2016 or Linux and lower there is additional integration that needs to be switched on and agents need to be aligned.  NOTE: "Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE)" was formerly known as "Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection (WDATP)." There are a number of places (e.g. Azure CLI) where the "WDATP" acronym is still used within Azure.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, Endpoint protection is `off`.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Agentless scanning for machines' Component Status is Set to 'On'

Attributes.Description: Using disk snapshots, the agentless scanner scans for installed software, vulnerabilities, and plain text secrets.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: The Microsoft Defender for Cloud agentless machine scanner provides threat detection, vulnerability detection, and discovery of sensitive information.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Agentless scanning for machines requires licensing and is included in Defender CSPM and in Defender for Servers Plan 2. Each machine is scanned once every 24 hours, and only while it is running.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From the Azure Portal `Home` page, select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud` 2. Under `Management` select `Environment Settings` 3. Select a subscription 4. Under `Settings` > `Defender Plans`, click `Settings & monitoring` 5. Under the Component column, locate the row for `Agentless scanning for machines` 6. Select `On` 7. Click `Continue` in the top left 8. Select `Save`  Repeat the above for any additional subscriptions.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  This command sets Defender for Servers to Plan 2 and turns the component on. Before running it, run the audit command and add one `--extensions name=<extension-name> isEnabled=<True-or-False>` argument for each other extension it lists, so that their settings are unchanged.  ``` az security pricing create --name VirtualMachines --tier Standard --subplan P2 --extensions name=AgentlessVmScanning isEnabled=True ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  This command sets Defender for Servers to Plan 2 and turns the component on. Before running it, run the audit command and add an entry to the `-Extension` array for each other extension it lists, so that their settings are unchanged.  ``` Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'VirtualMachines' -PricingTier 'Standard' -SubPlan 'P2' -Extension '[{"name":"AgentlessVmScanning","isEnabled":"True","additionalExtensionProperties":null}]' ```  Where Defender CSPM provides the component instead of Defender for Servers Plan 2, use the Azure Portal procedure. `Set-AzSecurityPricing` does not enable the Defender CSPM agentless extensions.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From the Azure Portal `Home` page, select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud` 2. Under `Management` select `Environment Settings` 3. Select a subscription 4. Under `Settings` > `Defender Plans`, click `Settings & monitoring` 5. Under the Component column, locate the row for `Agentless scanning for machines` 6. Ensure that `On` is selected  Repeat the above for any additional subscriptions.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following commands for each subscription:  ``` az security pricing show --name VirtualMachines --subscription <subscription-id> --query "{tier:pricingTier, subPlan:subPlan, agentlessScanning:extensions[?name=='AgentlessVmScanning'].isEnabled | [0]}" az security pricing show --name CloudPosture --subscription <subscription-id> --query "{tier:pricingTier, agentlessScanning:extensions[?name=='AgentlessVmScanning'].isEnabled | [0]}" ```  The component passes when at least one of the two commands returns a `tier` of `Standard` and an `agentlessScanning` value of `True`. For the `VirtualMachines` command, `subPlan` must also be `P2`.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command for each subscription:  ``` foreach ($plan in 'VirtualMachines', 'CloudPosture') { $pricing = Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name $plan $agentless = $pricing.Extensions | ConvertFrom-Json | Where-Object { $_.name -eq 'AgentlessVmScanning' } [pscustomobject]@{ Plan = $plan; PricingTier = $pricing.PricingTier; SubPlan = $pricing.SubPlan; AgentlessVmScanning = $agentless.isEnabled } } ```  The component passes when at least one row shows a `PricingTier` of `Standard` and an `AgentlessVmScanning` value of `True`. For the `VirtualMachines` row, `SubPlan` must also be `P2`.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Agentless scanning has one setting for each subscription, and either Defender for Servers Plan 2 or Defender CSPM can provide it. The audit passes when either plan has the component on. The component is on by default when Defender for Servers Plan 2 is enabled.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, Agentless scanning for machines is `off`.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'File Integrity Monitoring' Component Status is Set to 'On'

Attributes.Description: File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) examines operating system files, Windows registries, application software, and Linux system files for changes that might indicate an attack or compromise.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: FIM provides a detection mechanism for compromised files. When FIM is enabled, critical system files are monitored for changes that might indicate a threat actor is attempting to modify system files for lateral compromise within a host operating system.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: File Integrity Monitoring requires licensing and is included in Defender for Servers Plan 2. It also stores change events in a Log Analytics workspace, which is billed under its own pricing for data ingestion and retention.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From the Azure Portal `Home` page, select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud` 2. Under `Management` select `Environment Settings` 3. Select a subscription 4. Under `Settings` > `Defender Plans`, click `Settings & monitoring` 5. Under the Component column, locate the row for `File Integrity Monitoring` 6. Select `On` 7. Select `Edit configuration` and select the Log Analytics workspace that stores the change events, or select `Create new` 8. Select `Apply` 9. Click `Continue` in the top left 10. Select `Save`  Repeat the above for any additional subscriptions.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  This command sets Defender for Servers to Plan 2 and turns the component on. Before running it, run the audit command for `VirtualMachines` without the `--query` argument, and add one `--extensions name=<extension-name> isEnabled=<True-or-False>` argument for each other extension it lists, so that their settings are unchanged. This command does not select the Log Analytics workspace; select it in the Azure Portal as described above.  ``` az security pricing create --name VirtualMachines --tier Standard --subplan P2 --extensions name=FileIntegrityMonitoring isEnabled=True ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  This command sets Defender for Servers to Plan 2 and turns the component on. Before running it, run the PowerShell audit command and add an entry to the `-Extension` array for each other extension it lists, so that their settings are unchanged. This command does not select the Log Analytics workspace; select it in the Azure Portal as described above.  ``` Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'VirtualMachines' -PricingTier 'Standard' -SubPlan 'P2' -Extension '[{"name":"FileIntegrityMonitoring","isEnabled":"True","additionalExtensionProperties":null}]' ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From the Azure Portal `Home` page, select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud` 2. Under `Management` select `Environment Settings` 3. Select a subscription 4. Under `Settings` > `Defender Plans`, click `Settings & monitoring` 5. Under the Component column, locate the row for `File Integrity Monitoring` 6. Ensure that `On` is selected  Repeat the above for any additional subscriptions.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command for each subscription:  ``` az security pricing show --name VirtualMachines --subscription <subscription-id> --query "{tier:pricingTier, subPlan:subPlan, fileIntegrityMonitoring:extensions[?name=='FileIntegrityMonitoring'].isEnabled | [0]}" ```  Verify that `tier` is `Standard`, `subPlan` is `P2`, and `fileIntegrityMonitoring` is `True`.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following command for each subscription:  ``` $pricing = Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'VirtualMachines' $fim = $pricing.Extensions | ConvertFrom-Json | Where-Object { $_.name -eq 'FileIntegrityMonitoring' } [pscustomobject]@{ PricingTier = $pricing.PricingTier; SubPlan = $pricing.SubPlan; FileIntegrityMonitoring = $fim.isEnabled } ```  Verify that `PricingTier` is `Standard`, `SubPlan` is `P2`, and `FileIntegrityMonitoring` is `True`.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: File Integrity Monitoring stores change events in a Log Analytics workspace and collects data through the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent, which must be version 10.8799 or later on legacy Windows machines and 30.124082 or later on Linux. The component is not on by default when Defender for Servers Plan 2 is enabled.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, File Integrity Monitoring is `Off`.

Requirements.Description: Ensure That Microsoft Defender for Containers Is Set To 'On'

Attributes.Description: Microsoft Defender for Containers helps improve, monitor, and maintain the security of containerized assets—including Kubernetes clusters, nodes, workloads, container registries, and images—across multi-cloud and on-premises environments.  By default, when enabling the plan through the Azure Portal, Microsoft Defender for Containers automatically configures the following components:  - `Agentless scanning for machines` - `Defender sensor` for runtime protection - `Azure Policy` for enforcing security best practices - `K8S API access` for monitoring and threat detection - `Registry access` for vulnerability assessment  **Note:** Microsoft Defender for Container Registries ('ContainerRegistry') is deprecated and has been replaced by Microsoft Defender for Containers ('Containers').
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Enabling Microsoft Defender for Containers enhances defense-in-depth by providing advanced threat detection, vulnerability assessment, and security monitoring for containerized environments, leveraging insights from the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC).
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Microsoft Defender for Containers incurs a charge per vCore. Refer to https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/defender-for-cloud/ and https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/calculator/ to estimate potential costs.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment settings`. 3. Click the name of a subscription. 4. Under `Settings`, click `Defender plans`. 5. Under `Cloud Workload Protection (CWP)`, in the row for `Containers`, click `On` in the `Status` column. 6. If `Monitoring coverage` displays `Partial`, click `Settings` under `Partial`. 7. Set the status of each of the components to `On`. 8. Click `Continue`. 9. Click `Save`. 10. Repeat steps 1-9 for each subscription.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  **Note:** Microsoft Defender for Container Registries ('ContainerRegistry') is deprecated and has been replaced by Microsoft Defender for Containers ('Containers').  Run the below command to enable the Microsoft Defender for Containers plan and its components:  ``` az security pricing create -n 'Containers' --tier 'standard' --extensions name=ContainerRegistriesVulnerabilityAssessments isEnabled=True --extensions name=AgentlessDiscoveryForKubernetes isEnabled=True --extensions name=AgentlessVmScanning isEnabled=True --extensions name=ContainerSensor isEnabled=True ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  **Note:** Microsoft Defender for Container Registries ('ContainerRegistry') is deprecated and has been replaced by Microsoft Defender for Containers ('Containers').  Run the below command to enable the Microsoft Defender for Containers plan and its components:  ``` Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'Containers' -PricingTier 'Standard' -Extension '[{"name":"ContainerRegistriesVulnerabilityAssessments","isEnabled":"True"},{"name":"AgentlessDiscoveryForKubernetes","isEnabled":"True"},{"name":"AgentlessVmScanning","isEnabled":"True"},{"name":"ContainerSensor","isEnabled":"True"}]' ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment settings`. 3. Click the name of a subscription. 4. Under `Settings`, click `Defender plans`. 5. Under `Cloud Workload Protection (CWP)`, in the row for `Containers`, ensure that the `Status` is set to `On` and `Monitoring coverage` displays `Full`. 6. Repeat steps 1-5 for each subscription.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  For Microsoft Defender for Container Registries (deprecated), run the following command:  ``` az security pricing show --name "ContainerRegistry" --query pricingTier ```  Ensure that the command returns `Standard`.  For Microsoft Defender for Containers, run the following command:  ``` az security pricing show --name "Containers" --query [pricingTier,extensions[*].[name,isEnabled]] ```  Ensure that the command returns `Standard`, and that each of the extensions (ContainerRegistriesVulnerabilityAssessments, AgentlessDiscoveryForKubernetes, AgentlessVmScanning, ContainerSensor) returns `True`.  Repeat for each subscription.  **Audit from PowerShell**  For Microsoft Defender for Container Registries (deprecated), run the following command:  ``` Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'ContainerRegistry' | Select-Object Name,PricingTier ```  Ensure the command returns `PricingTier` `Standard`.  For Microsoft Defender for Containers, run the following command:  ``` Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'Containers' ```  Ensure that `PricingTier` is set to `Standard`, and that each of the extensions (ContainerRegistriesVulnerabilityAssessments, AgentlessDiscoveryForKubernetes, AgentlessVmScanning, ContainerSensor) has `isEnabled` set to `True`.  Repeat for each subscription.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [1c988dd6-ade4-430f-a608-2a3e5b0a6d38](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F1c988dd6-ade4-430f-a608-2a3e5b0a6d38) **- Name:** 'Microsoft Defender for Containers should be enabled'
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: The Azure Policy 'Microsoft Defender for Containers should be enabled' checks only that the `pricingTier` for `Containers` is set to `Standard`. It does not check the status of the plan's components.
Attributes.DefaultValue: The Microsoft Defender for Containers plan is disabled by default.

Requirements.Description: Ensure That Microsoft Defender for Azure Cosmos DB Is Set To 'On'

Requirements.Description: Ensure That Microsoft Defender for AI Services Is Set To 'On'

Attributes.Description: Turning on Microsoft Defender for AI Services enables threat protection for Azure OpenAI and Azure AI model inference workloads in Microsoft Foundry, providing runtime detection of threats such as prompt injection attacks, data leakage, and credential theft in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Enabling Microsoft Defender for AI Services allows for greater defense-in-depth. It continuously analyzes activity on supported Azure OpenAI and Azure AI model inference deployments and generates context-based security alerts for threats such as jailbreak, data leakage, and credential theft, drawing on Microsoft threat intelligence and Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Turning on Microsoft Defender for AI Services incurs an additional cost based on the number of tokens scanned. A 30-day free trial is available, capped at 75 billion tokens scanned; billing begins once that cap is reached or the trial period ends.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, select `Environment Settings`. 3. Click on the subscription name. 4. Select the `Defender plans` blade. 5. Select `On` under `Status` for `AI services`. 6. Select `Save`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Enable the Standard pricing tier for AI services:  ``` az security pricing create -n 'AI' --tier 'Standard' ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Enable the Standard pricing tier for AI services:  ``` Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'AI' -PricingTier 'Standard' ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, select `Environment Settings`. 3. Click on the subscription name. 4. Select the `Defender plans` blade. 5. Ensure `Status` is set to `On` for `AI services`.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Ensure the output of the below command is `Standard`  ``` az security pricing show -n 'AI' --query 'pricingTier' ```  **Audit from PowerShell**  ``` Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'AI' | Select-Object Name,PricingTier ```  Ensure the output for `PricingTier` is `Standard`  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [c2c0c6d8-007b-4a48-8d9b-3539bddd8e87](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2Fc2c0c6d8-007b-4a48-8d9b-3539bddd8e87) **- Name:** 'Microsoft Defender for AI Services should be enabled'
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: At the time of writing, threat protection for AI services is available in Azure commercial clouds only; it is not offered in Azure Government or Microsoft Azure operated by 21Vianet. Enabling the plan also requires Microsoft Defender for Cloud to be enabled on the subscription. The plan covers supported Azure OpenAI and Azure AI model inference models and scans text tokens only; image and audio tokens are not scanned. Even when the subscription-level plan is set to the Standard tier, an individual AI resource can be opted out by setting its `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/defenderForAISettings` state to `Disabled` — a condition the subscription-level audit above does not detect, so review resource-level settings where full coverage is required.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, the Microsoft Defender for AI Services plan is off.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Suspicious prompt evidence' Component Status is Set to 'On'

Attributes.Description: Microsoft Defender for AI Services alerts either include the suspicious segments of user prompts and model responses as evidence, with sensitive data redacted, or mask that content. The `Enable user prompt evidence` setting of the plan's suspicious prompt evidence component selects between them, with values `On` and `Off`.  **Prerequisites:** Complete the recommendation `Ensure That Microsoft Defender for AI Services Is Set To 'On'` first, because this component can be configured only while the plan is on.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: With the component off, Defender for Cloud still detects AI threats but masks prompt and response content in alerts, so analysts cannot see what was sent to the model or what it returned. A jailbreak or data-leakage alert then cannot be confirmed or scoped from its evidence, delaying response and obscuring what data was disclosed.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Once on, alert evidence contains redacted snippets of user prompts and model responses. These are customer data, visible to anyone who can read the alerts in the Azure portal, the Defender portal, or an attached partner integration, which can conflict with data-minimization requirements.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Note:** These steps require the Owner or Contributor role on each subscription. The Azure CLI and PowerShell commands set the plan to `Standard`, which turns it on where it is off.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud` > `Environment settings`. 2. Click the name of a subscription. 3. On the `Defender plans` page, locate `AI services` and click `Settings`. 4. Set `Enable user prompt evidence` to `On`. 5. Click `Continue`. 6. Click `Save`. 7. Repeat steps 1-6 for each subscription.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Run the following command for each subscription. For each other extension the Audit listed, repeat `--extensions` with its name, current `isEnabled` value, and any `additionalExtensionProperties` so the update leaves it unchanged.  ``` az security pricing create -n 'AI' --tier 'Standard' --subscription <subscription-id> --extensions name=AIPromptEvidence isEnabled=True ```  **Remediate from PowerShell**  Run the following commands for each subscription. They set `AIPromptEvidence` to `True`, adding it if absent, and resubmit the plan's other extensions unchanged.  ``` Set-AzContext -Subscription <subscription-id> $extensions = @(((Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'AI').Extensions | ConvertFrom-Json) | Select-Object name, isEnabled, additionalExtensionProperties) $row = $extensions | Where-Object { $_.name -eq 'AIPromptEvidence' } if ($row) { $row.isEnabled = 'True' } else { $extensions += [pscustomobject]@{ name = 'AIPromptEvidence'; isEnabled = 'True'; additionalExtensionProperties = $null } } Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'AI' -PricingTier 'Standard' -Extension (ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $extensions -Compress -Depth 5) ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Navigate to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud` > `Environment settings`. 2. Click the name of a subscription. 3. On the `Defender plans` page, locate `AI services` and click `Settings`. 4. Verify that `Enable user prompt evidence` is set to `On`. 5. Repeat steps 1-4 for each subscription.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command for each subscription:  ``` az security pricing show -n 'AI' --subscription <subscription-id> --query "extensions[].{Name:name, IsEnabled:isEnabled}" --output table ```  The subscription is compliant when the `AIPromptEvidence` row shows `True`. A value of `False`, or no `AIPromptEvidence` row, is non-compliant.  **Audit from PowerShell**  Run the following commands for each subscription:  ``` Set-AzContext -Subscription <subscription-id> ((Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name 'AI').Extensions | ConvertFrom-Json) | Select-Object name, isEnabled ```  The subscription is compliant when the `AIPromptEvidence` row shows `True`. A value of `False`, or no `AIPromptEvidence` row, is non-compliant.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Plan management in the Microsoft Defender portal is in preview. After a subscription's plan management moves there, plan settings are view-only in the Azure portal, so configure this component in the Defender portal's AI services plan settings instead. The built-in Azure Policy 'Configure Microsoft Defender threat protection for AI Services' can enforce this component through DeployIfNotExists, but its default parameters also enable data security for AI interactions, a preview feature that requires a separate Microsoft Purview license.
Attributes.DefaultValue: Microsoft does not document the default state of this component; confirm it with the Audit Procedure.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that Microsoft Defender for Cloud is Configured to Check VM Operating Systems for Updates

Attributes.Description: Defender for Cloud reports missing operating system updates on machines from Azure Update Manager assessment data. A machine's periodic assessment setting is `ImageDefault`, which runs no scheduled check, or `AutomaticByPlatform`, which checks for missing updates every 24 hours.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: A machine that is never assessed has no record of the security updates it lacks. It stays exploitable through every published vulnerability it is missing a patch for, with no recommendation or alert to prompt anyone to fix it.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Defender for Cloud generates the system update recommendations only on subscriptions with Defender for Servers Plan 2, which is billed per machine; see https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/defender-for-cloud/. Without Plan 2, periodic assessment of Azure Arc-enabled machines incurs Azure Update Manager charges. Installing updates can restart machines, depending on the reboot setting chosen for the installation.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Select `Recommendations`. 3. Select `Machines should be configured to periodically check for missing system updates`. 4. Select the unhealthy machines, then click `Fix`. 5. Select `System updates should be installed on your machines (powered by Azure Update Manager)`. 6. Select the unhealthy machines, then click `Fix` to install the missing updates.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  For each Windows virtual machine requiring remediation, run the following command:  ``` az vm update --resource-group <resource-group> --name <vm-name> --set osProfile.windowsConfiguration.patchSettings.assessmentMode=AutomaticByPlatform ```  For each Linux virtual machine requiring remediation, run the following command:  ``` az vm update --resource-group <resource-group> --name <vm-name> --set osProfile.linuxConfiguration.patchSettings.assessmentMode=AutomaticByPlatform ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Select `Recommendations`. 3. Search for `Machines should be configured to periodically check for missing system updates`. 4. Verify that no machines are listed as unhealthy. 5. Search for `System updates should be installed on your machines (powered by Azure Update Manager)`. The cited Azure Policy definition keeps the earlier name, powered by Update Center. 6. Verify that no machines are listed as unhealthy.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command for each Azure virtual machine:  ``` az vm show --resource-group <resource-group> --name <vm-name> --query "{windows:osProfile.windowsConfiguration.patchSettings.assessmentMode, linux:osProfile.linuxConfiguration.patchSettings.assessmentMode}" ```  Verify that the value for the machine's operating system is `AutomaticByPlatform`. This command checks only the periodic assessment setting on Azure VMs; use the portal method for Azure Arc-enabled machines and for installed updates.  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [f85bf3e0-d513-442e-89c3-1784ad63382b](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2Ff85bf3e0-d513-442e-89c3-1784ad63382b) **- Name:** 'System updates should be installed on your machines (powered by Update Center)' - **Policy ID:** [bd876905-5b84-4f73-ab2d-2e7a7c4568d9](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2Fbd876905-5b84-4f73-ab2d-2e7a7c4568d9) **- Name:** 'Machines should be configured to periodically check for missing system updates'
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Both cited Azure Policy definitions report compliance with audit effects: `AuditIfNotExists` for the system updates definition and `Audit` for the periodic check definition. Organizations that assess and install updates with a different patch management tool may meet the intent of this recommendation with that tool.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, periodic assessment is `ImageDefault`, and no scheduled update check runs.

Requirements.Description: Ensure Continuous Export of Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts is configured to a SIEM

Attributes.Description: Configuring an alert monitoring and response process ensures that alerts are actioned in a timely manner. Integrate with SIEM solutions like Microsoft Sentinel, or configure email/webhook notifications to security teams.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Continuous monitoring and alert triage ensure that detected threats are acted upon quickly, reducing risk exposure.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Requires integration effort with SIEM or alerting tools and a defined incident response process. The cost incurred depends on the volume of exported alerts and the destination service.  For more details on pricing models with Log Analytics and Event Hubs:  - Log Analytics: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/cost-logs#pricing-model - Event Hubs: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/event-hubs/
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  Connect Microsoft Defender for Cloud to a SIEM such as Microsoft Sentinel or another log analytics solution.  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment Settings`. 3. Expand the Tenant Root Group(s) to reveal subscriptions.  For each subscription listed:  1. Click the subscription name to open the `Defender Plans` settings 2. In the settings on the left, click `Continuous Export` 3. Select `Event Hub`, `Log Analytics Workspace`, or both depending on your environment. 4. Set `Export enabled` to `On` 5. Under Exported data types, ensure that **at least** `Security Alerts (Medium and High)` is checked. 6. Under Export target, set the target Event Hub or Log Analytics Workspace which is tied to a SIEM that is configured to monitor and alert for security alerts.  Ensure security alerts are included in the security operations workflow and incident response plan.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. Go to `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 2. Under `Management`, click `Environment Settings`. 3. Expand the Tenant Root Group(s) to reveal subscriptions.  For each subscription listed:  1. Click the subscription name to open the `Defender Plans` settings 2. In the settings on the left, click `Continuous Export`  Ensure that `Export enabled` is set to `On` and delivering **at least** `Security Alerts (Medium and High)` to an Event Hub or Log Analytics Workspace which is tied to a SIEM that is configured to monitor and alert for security alerts.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, continuous export is `Off`.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that non-deprecated Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark policies are not set to 'Disabled'

Attributes.Description: The Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB) is an Azure Policy initiative automatically assigned to all subscriptions that evaluates resource configurations against Microsoft security best practice recommendations. Policies set to a `Disabled` effect are not evaluated, removing visibility into the associated recommendation. Microsoft deprecates policies when controls are superseded or no longer applicable; deprecated policies are set to `Disabled` by default and require no corrective action. Non-deprecated policies should not be set to `Disabled` without a documented organizational exception.  **Note:** A policy is considered deprecated when its definition name is prefixed with `[Deprecated]:` in the Azure Policy portal and its `policyDeprecated` metadata property is `true`.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Disabling a non-deprecated MCSB policy prevents Microsoft Defender for Cloud from evaluating the associated control and surfacing relevant recommendations, creating an undetected gap in security posture visibility. Exceptions allowing non-deprecated MCSB policies to be disabled can be reasonably made but each exception should be documented and reconsidered periodically.  **Examples of reasonable exceptions:**  - A compensating control exists which cannot be evaluated by the policy - A scope exemption exists for certain resources within the evaluated scope - The policy effect conflicts with architecturally deliberate choices - The resource type is not used in the evaluated scope  Deprecated policies set to `Disabled` reflect an intentional Microsoft lifecycle decision and are not a finding.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: MCSB policies default to an `Audit` or `AuditIfNotExists` effect, which evaluates but does not enforce recommendations. Re-enabling a non-deprecated disabled policy restores evaluation only; no enforcement action occurs unless the effect is subsequently changed to `Deny` or `DeployIfNotExists` by the administrator.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: No remediation is required for deprecated MCSB policies set to `Disabled`.  For non-deprecated policies found to be set to `Disabled`, restore the effect to its default value or document an approved organizational exception.  **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home, select the Portal Menu. 2. Select **Microsoft Defender for Cloud**. 3. Under **Management**, select **Environment settings**. 4. Click on the appropriate Management Group or Subscription. 5. Click **Security policies** in the left column. 6. Click **Microsoft cloud security benchmark**. 7. Click **Add filter**, select **Effect**, check **Disabled**, and click **Apply**. 8. Confirm the displayed policy is not deprecated before proceeding. 9. Click the blue ellipsis **...** to the right of the policy name and select **Manage effect and parameters**. 10. Under **Policy effect**, select **Audit**. 11. Click **Save**, then click **Refresh**. 12. Repeat steps 8–11 for each non-deprecated disabled policy. 13. Repeat steps 1–12 for each Management Group or Subscription requiring remediation.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  Perform the following steps for each Management Group or Subscription:  1. From Azure Home, select the Portal Menu. 2. Select **Microsoft Defender for Cloud**. 3. Under **Management**, select **Environment settings**. 4. Click on the appropriate Management Group or Subscription. 5. Click **Security policies** in the left column. 6. Click **Microsoft cloud security benchmark**. 7. Click **Add filter**, select **Effect**, check the **Disabled** box, and click **Apply**. 8. For each policy returned, confirm whether the definition is deprecated: - Deprecated definitions display a `[Deprecated]:` name prefix. - Deprecated policies set to `Disabled` are **expected and compliant**. 9. Verify that no non-deprecated policies are displayed with a `Disabled` effect. 10. Repeat steps 1–9 for each Management Group or Subscription.  Cross-reference each overridden policy against current documented exceptions and the Azure Policy definitions list to confirm deprecation status before treating the result as a finding.
Attributes.DefaultValue: The MCSB policy initiative is automatically assigned to all subscriptions with Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Of the **412** policies currently in the MCSB initiative, **0** have a default effect of `Disabled` and **0** are deprecated. Any policy found with a `Disabled` effect reflects an administrative override applied after the default assignment.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that Microsoft Defender for Cloud Sends Security Alert Emails to Users with the 'Owner' Role

Attributes.Description: Defender for Cloud alert emails go to the addresses in the subscription's security contact and, optionally, to every holder of selected subscription roles. The `All users with the following roles` setting selects any of `Owner`, `Contributor`, `ServiceAdmin`, and `AccountAdmin`.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Subscription owners hold the authority to contain an incident in the subscription. Without role-based notification, an alert about an active compromise can reach no one with that authority and sit unread in the portal while the attack continues.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Every user assigned the Owner role on the subscription receives the alert emails, so mail volume grows with the number of owners and with the severity threshold set by the recommendation `Ensure that 'Notify about alerts with the following severity (or higher)' is Enabled`.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment settings`. 4. Click the appropriate management group, subscription, or workspace. 5. Click `Email notifications`. 6. In the `All users with the following roles` drop-down, select `Owner`. 7. Click `Save`. 8. Repeat steps 1-7 for each subscription requiring remediation.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  For each subscription requiring remediation, save the current security contact, because the write below replaces the whole object:  ``` az rest --method get --uri "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<subscription-id>/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts/default?api-version=2023-12-01-preview" --query "{properties:properties}" > input.json ```  In `input.json`, add `Owner` to `notificationsByRole.roles` and set `state` to `On`, keeping every existing role, email, and notification source. The result has this shape:  ``` { "properties": { "emails": "<existing-email-addresses>", "isEnabled": true, "notificationsByRole": { "state": "On", "roles": ["Owner", "<existing-roles>"] }, "notificationsSources": [ { "sourceType": "Alert", "minimalSeverity": "<existing-severity>" }, { "sourceType": "AttackPath", "minimalRiskLevel": "<existing-risk-level>" } ] } } ```  Run the following command to write the edited contact back:  ``` az rest --method put --uri "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<subscription-id>/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts/default?api-version=2023-12-01-preview" --body @input.json ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment settings`. 4. Click the appropriate management group, subscription, or workspace. 5. Click `Email notifications`. 6. Verify that `All users with the following roles` includes `Owner`. 7. Repeat steps 1-6 for each subscription.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Run the following command to read the security contact of every enabled subscription visible to the signed-in account:  ``` for sub in $(az account list --query "[?state=='Enabled'].id" --output tsv); do az rest --method get --uri "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$sub/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts?api-version=2023-12-01-preview" --query "value[?name=='default'].{id:id, isEnabled:properties.isEnabled, notificationsByRole:properties.notificationsByRole}" done ```  Verify that each subscription returns `isEnabled` as `true`, `notificationsByRole.state` as `On`, and `Owner` in `notificationsByRole.roles`. An empty result is non-compliant.
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: The `securityContacts` API has no generally available version, so the Azure CLI procedures use the current preview version, 2023-12-01-preview. The same security contact holds the settings checked by `Ensure 'Additional email addresses' is Configured with a Security Contact Email`, `Ensure that 'Notify about alerts with the following severity (or higher)' is Enabled`, and `Ensure that 'Notify about attack paths with the following risk level (or higher)' is Enabled`; a request that omits them clears them.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, `Owner` is selected

Requirements.Description: Ensure 'Additional email addresses' is Configured with a Security Contact Email

Attributes.Description: Microsoft Defender for Cloud emails the subscription owners whenever a high-severity alert is triggered for their subscription. You should provide a security contact email address as an additional email address.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Microsoft Defender for Cloud emails the Subscription Owner to notify them about security alerts. Adding your Security Contact's email address to the 'Additional email addresses' field ensures that your organization's Security Team is included in these alerts. This ensures that the proper people are aware of any potential compromise in order to mitigate the risk in a timely fashion.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment Settings`. 4. Click on the appropriate Management Group, Subscription, or Workspace. 5. Click on `Email notifications`. 6. Enter a valid security contact email address (or multiple addresses separated by commas) in the `Additional email addresses` field. 7. Click `Save`.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Use the below command to set `Security contact emails` to `On`.  ``` az account get-access-token --query "{subscription:subscription,accessToken:accessToken}" --out tsv | xargs -L1 bash -c 'curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$0/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts/default?api-version=2020-01-01-preview -d@"input.json"' ```  Where `input.json` contains the data below, replacing `validEmailAddress` with a single email address or multiple comma-separated email addresses:  ``` { "id": "/subscriptions/<Your_Subscription_Id>/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts/default", "name": "default", "type": "Microsoft.Security/securityContacts", "properties": { "email": "<validEmailAddress>", "alertNotifications": "On", "alertsToAdmins": "On" } } ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment Settings`. 4. Click on the appropriate Management Group, Subscription, or Workspace. 5. Click on `Email notifications`. 6. Ensure that a valid security contact email address is listed in the `Additional email addresses` field.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Ensure the output of the below command is not empty and is set with appropriate email ids:  ``` az account get-access-token --query "{subscription:subscription,accessToken:accessToken}" --out tsv | xargs -L1 bash -c 'curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$0/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts?api-version=2020-01-01-preview' | jq '.|.[] | select(.name=="default")'|jq '.properties.emails' ```  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [4f4f78b8-e367-4b10-a341-d9a4ad5cf1c7](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F4f4f78b8-e367-4b10-a341-d9a4ad5cf1c7) **- Name:** 'Subscriptions should have a contact email address for security issues'
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Excluding any entries in the `input.json` properties block disables the specific setting by default.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, there are no additional email addresses entered.

Requirements.Description: Ensure that 'Notify about alerts with the following severity (or higher)' is Enabled

Attributes.Description: Enables emailing security alerts to the subscription owner or other designated security contact.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Enabling security alert emails ensures that security alert emails are sent by Microsoft. This ensures that the right people are aware of any potential security issues and can mitigate the risk.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Enabling security alert emails can cause alert fatigue, increasing the risk of missing important alerts. Select an appropriate severity level to manage notifications. Azure aims to reduce alert fatigue by limiting the daily email volume per severity level. Learn more: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/configure-email-notifications#email-frequency.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: **Remediate from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment settings`. 4. Click on the appropriate Subscription. 5. Click on `Email notifications`. 6. Under `Notification types`, check box next to `Notify about alerts with the following severity (or higher)` and select an appropriate severity level from the drop-down menu. 7. Click `Save`. 8. Repeat steps 1-7 for each Subscription requiring remediation.  **Remediate from Azure CLI**  Use the below command to enable `Send email notification for high severity alerts`:  ``` az account get-access-token --query "{subscription:subscription,accessToken:accessToken}" --out tsv | xargs -L1 bash -c 'curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<$0>/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts/default1?api-version=2017-08-01-preview -d@"input.json"' ```  Where `input.json` contains the data below, replacing `validEmailAddress` with a single email address or multiple comma-separated email addresses:  ``` { "id": "/subscriptions/<subscriptionId>/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts/default", "name": "default", "type": "Microsoft.Security/securityContacts", "properties": { "email": "<validEmailAddress>", "alertNotifications": "On", "alertsToAdmins": "On" } } ```
Attributes.AuditProcedure: **Audit from Azure Portal**  1. From Azure Home select the Portal Menu. 2. Select `Microsoft Defender for Cloud`. 3. Under `Management`, select `Environment settings`. 4. Click on the appropriate Subscription. 5. Click on `Email notifications`. 6. Under `Notification types`, ensure that the box next to `Notify about alerts with the following severity (or higher)` is checked, and an appropriate severity level is selected. 7. Repeat steps 1-6 for each Subscription.  **Audit from Azure CLI**  Including a Subscription ID at the `$0` in `/subscriptions/$0/providers`, ensure the below command returns `"state": "On"`, and that `"minimalSeverity"` is set to an appropriate severity level:  ``` az account get-access-token --query "{subscription:subscription,accessToken:accessToken}" --out tsv | xargs -L1 bash -c 'curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$0/providers/Microsoft.Security/securityContacts?api-version=2020-01-01-preview' | jq '.|.[] | select(.name=="default")'|jq '.properties.alertNotifications' ```  **Audit from Azure Policy**  If referencing a digital copy of this Benchmark, clicking a Policy ID will open a link to the associated Policy definition in Azure.  If referencing a printed copy, you can search Policy IDs from this URL: https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyMenuBlade/~/Definitions  - **Policy ID:** [6e2593d9-add6-4083-9c9b-4b7d2188c899](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F6e2593d9-add6-4083-9c9b-4b7d2188c899) **- Name:** 'Email notification for high severity alerts should be enabled' - **Policy ID:** [0b15565f-aa9e-48ba-8619-45960f2c314d](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Policy/PolicyDetailBlade/definitionId/%2Fproviders%2FMicrosoft.Authorization%2FpolicyDefinitions%2F0b15565f-aa9e-48ba-8619-45960f2c314d) **- Name:** 'Email notification to subscription owner for high severity alerts should be enabled'
Attributes.AdditionalInformation: Excluding any entries in the `input.json` properties block disables the specific setting by default. This recommendation has been updated to reflect recent changes to Microsoft REST APIs for getting and updating security contact information.
Attributes.DefaultValue: By default, subscription owners receive email notifications for high-severity alerts.
